Scene VI: Confusius Maximus

The Sapari Tavern, Sapari
The 1stDay of the 4th Moon, 1536 P.V.

Allyra arrived at the Sapari Tavern just before midday. The rustic public house was quiet with just a few men sitting along the chipped, wooden bar, which ran the length of the tavern, and a few families seated quietly in the wooden booths opposite. The drink of choice, mulled cider, spread a potent ambience about the lounge to accompany the sounds of the men talking shit and laughing far too loudly. Wafts of smoke from Ashurrel leaf and cigars also stifled and stunk out the inn. Overall, the environment was a feast for the soul if the soul enjoys immense suffocation.

The owners, John and Jaeli Montgomery, were out for the day, so Allyra approached the barmaid, Charmaine. Charmaine was a small blonde lady with ridiculously large curves that seemed to have had an argument with her saucy red dress. The dress complained constantly about the poor fitting, and on occasion the laces would bust open of their own accord giving everyone an eyeful of Charmaine’s portly breasts. This embarrassed Charmaine and she would quickly try to force her flesh back into the upper corset of the gown. The men at the bar did not object to the floor show, although they often asked how she could possibly breathe. Charmaine would laugh, blow them a kiss, and continue to wear the wayward garment regardless of it inhibiting her lung capacity.

Allyra squished between two old, balding men, who’s cigars needed flicking, and addressed Charmaine directly,
‘Char, has Lord Fontacue checked in?’
Charmaine, who was bored with the bar room banter looked up from her game of Solitaire,
‘‘Ello Lyra, take a seat. I will be with you in a minute.’

Allyra looked up and down the bar, and picked a depressed, three-legged stool at the far end, which offered quick and subtle access to the stairs, so that she could meet her mark without everyone pointing out what a trollop she was.

Charmaine abandoned her punters and slowly followed Allyra to the far end of the bar. Once Allyra had sat down, a difficulty given the tightness of her shiny black leather catsuit, Charmaine leaned across the bar,
‘I need to speak to you,’ she whispered, then yelled, ‘WHAT can I get you?’ To divert the unwanted attention of any nosey punters.

The men did not look up as they were too engrossed in their discussion about whether the monster of the Twin Lakes, of which there was only one lake, could travel via land to the Getsug Sea. The conversation was largely redundant as the mythical beast was known to be a freshwater monster, not a saltwater monster.

Immortalis Book One: The Jester and The Immoless
Act One

Scene V: The Duplicitous Baers

The 1st Day of the 4th Moon, 1536 P.V.
Corax Asylum, Togaduine

Two beings rode towards the gates of Corax. One was a large, heavy-set man wearing a wolf skin cloak. From his thick, tan leather pants swung a sheathed dagger, and his dunn carried a shield on his behalf. His greying beard swallowed up the fair skin beneath masking world-weary wrinkles and scars.

His partner’s appearance contrasted with his. She was stunningly swarthy with flowing locks of curly black hair that matched her eyes and she wore a shredded dress soaked in elaborate brown and blue swirls. Her tiara matched her dress, and she too carried a blade at her side.

The gates flung themselves open welcoming the duo.

They cantered across the barren grounds to the front of the asylum where they were met by two porters dressed in orange and green overalls. The young gentlemen helped the couple down and led their horses away to be fed and have their thirsts quenched.

The arched oak door of the asylum was also open, and a Nicolai dressed in black, sporting long flowing brown locks met them.
‘You must be BaerNedi, and…’ He took the woman’s hand and kissed it, ‘Banshee Baer, your beauty is only preceded by its reputation.’
Banshee Baer smiled, took a double take whilst considering the implication of his words, then smiled again,
‘And which Nicolas are you?’ She asked.
‘Nicolai-Nicolas Nachtvinsky. I am afraid Chives could not meet you. He has gone to Sapari to collect Nicolas’s new suit.’
‘That’s fine.’ Banshee nodded, ‘Will Nicolas be joining us today?’
‘Unfortunately, not, Madam, he is allegedly writing a book with Nicolai-Binky, but to be honest I suspect he is sulking in his office as yesterday’s tribute-brain upset his stomach,’ Nachtvinsky lied. ‘Trust me, you would not want to be in the same room as him right now. Archie has Ball on standby to clean up any leakage.’

Ball was Nicolas’s favourite mutant, and he kept Ball in Corax with a rag or towel attached to him so that the monstrous ball could roll around clearing up noxious messes on demand.

‘Now,’ Nachtvinsky smiled, ‘I was just in the middle of writing the Corax national anthem when Nicolai-Archie asked me to fetch you, so follow me.’
Banshee and BaerNedi followed the maestro as he hummed an awful, off-key melody to himself. They bypassed the office, which had two Nicolai standing temporarily wedged in the doorway to block their view, then walked by the banqueting hall and headed south.

After passing several doors, who’s locksets offered joyous grins to welcome them, Nachtvinsky stopped at a rickety archway covered with a yellow and black plaid curtain,
‘In there,’ he gestured, ‘they are waiting for you.’

Banshee pulled the curtain aside and the rail shuddered. The two walked into the not-so-secret games room. The room matched the general damp and fungal aesthetic of the overall asylum. There were books, plates and papers strewn about the floor, some of which had their own sporous communities, and in the centre of the room an old, neglected teak table wobbled and groaned.

Four beings sat around the table playing games.

The first to speak was Nicolai-Archie. His name was not really Archie. Archie had no name as he was far too good for a proper noun. By trade he was an architect, so Nicolas called him Archie, and the Nicolai followed suit. Archie wore a splendid bright red and black, flamboyant suit covered in diamonds. His hat matched his suit and flourished with feathers. A monocle perched on his right eye,
‘Come, sit, our illustrious baers,’ he said, whilst gesturing to some empty chairs that pulled themselves out invitingly on the other side of the table.

The baers took their places at the table.

Opposite Archie slumped a masked figure wearing a burgundy and purple cloak and hood. On the table between Archie and the hooded figure sat a chessboard.
‘Elyas and I are partaking in a game of wits,’ Archie explained, ‘Elyas is losing.’
‘You’re cheating,’ Elyas replied.

This comment prompted the gentleman in the purple suit and hat, which sat next to Archie, to speak up,
‘No, Elyas, you’re cheating.’ The red-haired gentleman, Nicolai-Chester said as he pulled a deck of cards from his pocket.

Chester dealt seven cards to himself, and then seven cards to the third Nicolai at the table, Nicolai-Nicolas Remdali.

Remdali considered himself an artist and wore an oversized top hat sporting a melted pocket watch, and a suit patterned with embroidered pocket watches to match. His moustache was long and curled at the ends and he spoke with a stupid and clearly phoney accent,
‘Whata are we-a playing, mio amico?’
‘Rummy,’ Chester spat, ‘me first.’

Archie turned and looked at Chester’s cards, as he did, Elyas pinched Archie’s rook and hid it under the table.

Banshee’s eyes widened, but she said nothing about Elyas’s cheeky move, instead opting to ask,
‘Archie, Sir, I thought Elyas was banned from Corax?’
Archie turned back, looked at the board narrowing his eyes, then glared at Elyas,
‘Nicolas is indisposed today, Banshee, and what he does not know does not hurt him!’

Chester picked up a card and added his own two penny’s worth,
‘He’s got the shits.’
‘He is indisposed,’ Archie reiterated as he waved his hand towards Elyas, ‘as this necromancer will be if he does not return my rook.’
‘I don’t have your rook!’ Elyas bit back.
Archie growled and then hissed,
‘I will count to three… One.’

‘Umm,’ BaerNedi interrupted, ‘you summoned us?’
‘Si!’ Remdali replied putting down a joker for no reason in the world. Chester sighed, but said nothing, and instead laid a blank card.
‘We ‘ave a presento for you,’ Remdali continued.
‘Indeed, we do!’ Archie concurred, as Elyas put his rook on the wrong square, ‘We have a Mica.’

‘What’s a Mica?’ Banshee asked.
‘Not what, who?’ Chester replied, picking up his own blank card as Elyas moved the knight diagonally across the board.
‘Mica,’ Archie continued, ‘is a vampire, and he has been selected by Nicolas to betray Nicolas to our third Immoless.’

Chester glanced at the mirror on the wall behind Remdali, who desperately needed the ace of spades, rummaged through the pile, and took the card for himself. Archie responded by moving his king forward six spaces.

‘Do you know how to play these games?’ Banshee asked curiously.

The Nicolai and Elyas all stopped what they were doing and stared at her. They leaned forward in their chairs and drew their lips back. The candles dimmed.

Banshee let out a cough,
‘I, I was joking,’ she stuttered, ‘of course you do. I’m sorry.’
Chester grunted a single syllable indicative of a laugh, the candles glowed brightly, and the players resumed their games. Banshee tried to quell an involuntary sigh of relief,
‘Tell us about Mica.’
‘Who?’ Chester asked.
‘Mica.’
‘Who?’
Banshee looked towards Archie, who moved his bishop six steps forward and one to the left. Elyas responded with a gallant move, sacrificing his king to save the queen. The queen did not need saving and was very surprised when the king threw himself off the board and onto Chester’s messy heap of cards, which Remdali was flicking about in circles.

‘Mica,’ Archie said after an awkward silence, ‘is a vampire, and you shall take him to the Immoless. He will be her next victim. He has been supplied with enough information; tell her you found him wandering about some forest or another.’
‘We shall set this up exactly as Nicolas has advised,’ Banshee nodded reassuringly.
‘You had better,’ Chester growled. He then sniffed twice and added
‘Now, you girl, come here?’

Banshee went to stand when the curtain opened and a malnourished and blood-stained tribute with patches of her lank red-hair missing walked in. Her head hung and she looked at the floor. She shifted slowly, with a slight limp, and knelt before Chester,
‘Yes Sir?’
Chester pulled her to her feet. A long black tongue drooled from his mouth and licked her all over, then withdrew, happy with its exploration.

Chester pressed her back to her knees and whispered,
‘Fetch Mica!’
‘Yes Sir,’ the woman replied. She stood slowly, her eyes downcast, and backed out of the archway.

‘How did you know she was there?’ Banshee asked.
Chester glared at her. Archie glared at her, and both spoke at once in a low, unified voice,
‘Don’t ever question me again.’

Banshee lowered her head.
‘Forgive her,’ BaerNedi pleaded, ‘she forgets herself at times.’
Chester nodded,
‘Forgiven but not forgotten.’
Banshee shivered.

Mica arrived alone. He waited at the opened aperture until summoned by a click of Chester’s finger and thumb.
‘Buongiorno,’ Remdali said, laying two cards at once, ‘it’s-a your time. A.’
Mica bowed,
‘Am I to suffer the boiling?’
‘Si,’ Remdali replied as Chester picked up three cards, and Elyas jumped Archie’s knight with a pawn.

Mica folded his arms tightly across his body. Silence filled the room as Archie and Remdali simultaneously stared at the vampire. Chester spoke first,
‘We know what you are,’
‘Thinking,’ Archie continued, ‘fear of pain. Fear of death. Potential escape.’
‘But we promise you,’ Remdali butted in, ‘much worse awaits traitors.’
‘Even Irkalla can’t hide a traitor,’ Chester muttered.

‘I understand,’ Mica replied.
‘We can give him something to alleviate the pain,’ Banshee suggested, her head still lowered.
‘No!’ Archie and Chester snapped, ‘Bring the pain.’
‘As you wish.’

Archie added three draught pieces to the board,
‘Now, about the third Immoless. How is she?’
Banshee breathed deeply through her nose,
‘She thinks she has an alcohol problem. She is prepared for her destiny, a little bit moody about dying, but prepared.’
‘And the blackouts?’
‘They continue.’
‘Yes, they do,’ Chester leered, ‘but tell me, does she love her boyfriend?’

Banshee bit her lip hard,
‘May I speak freely, Sir?’
‘No one is stopping you,’ Chester replied, collecting all cards and shuffling them, ‘we value honesty.’
‘She feels that love is not meant for her, and that her impending death is a barricade to it.’
‘That is-a logic, not-a sentimenta-a,’ Remdali said as he pulled a piece of parchment and pencil from his suit and drew two stick people.
‘Allyra is melancholy,’ Banshee whispered, ‘it is heart-breaking to watch.’
Chester nodded,
‘We appreciate your honesty, Banshee, but you must not get attached. This attachment concerns Nicolas. She will meet Nicolas soon, and then Nicolas will be responsible for her. She will no longer be your concern, remember where your loyalties lie.’ Chester then changed the subject, ‘I think her sex addiction is more than ready for us. She has had a good tutor in that regards.’
‘Indeed,’ Banshee replied.
Chester flicked his wrist in her direction,
‘You may depart now, and don’t forget to take Mica with you.’

Banshee and BaerNedi stood, bowed to each of the players, then walked backwards through the archway taking Mica with them through the sea of wailing inmates. Their horses were waiting for them outside. Banshee took Mica on her steed, and BaerNedi led the way back to Sapari.

The two Nicolai waited until the baers had departed, stepped away from the office door, and left Nicolas to grin wildly at the wall in his own time. Nicolas found the wall less insipid than the baers, and he knew Banshee’s growing fondness for Allyra was cause for concern.

Accused Canadian spy Jeffrey Delisle broke down and confessed during interrogation following his arrest on espionage charges in January 2012.

In the video clip Delisle can be heard to say, "I am so dead. I, everyone, my wife that I loved for so long, killed me. Killed me."

Delisle was serving in the Royal Canadian Navy when he walked into the Russian embassy in Ottawa in 2007. He offered to sell classified information to the GRU for $10,000. Delisle was in significant financial debt at the time and later claimed that on the same day he approached the Russians, he had learned his wife Jennifer had cheated on him.

After that, he began providing information on a monthly basis for the next few years. Delisle typically received $3,000 per delivery and provided a wide variety of very sensitive information to the GRU. The Canadian Security Intelligence Service reported this included signals intelligence information, personal data on intelligence community employees, reports from several classified databases which Delisle had access to as a normal part of his duties, and even information on foreign sources of intelligence information.

He also had access to “Five Eyes” intelligence, from a cooperative agreement between the US, Canada, United Kingdom, Australia, and New Zealand, and therefore was able to pass the GRU intelligence gathered by five different nations.

The arrest sent shockwaves through the Canadian government and led to major changes in their own security and counterintelligence doctrine. Delisle had displayed many of the traditional indicators of espionage including unmanageable financial debt, frequent foreign travel, and accessing information outside the scope of his duties. But he went undiscovered for nearly five years. Afterwards, the facility he’d worked in at Halifax was virtually stripped down and rebuilt to determine if he’d installed any devices on behalf of the GRU or installed any programs on the digital network there.

In 2013 Delisle pleaded guilty to three espionage charges and was sentenced to 18 years in prison. He was released after just six years based on good behavior while confined.

If your peace depends on the security of digital vaults, the perfection of modern transport, or the stability of world governments, you will live in perpetual agitation.

Over the past week, the global news cycle delivered a staggering, multi-front reminder of human limitation: In the digital realm, hackers executed the largest financial theft in human history, draining $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance in minutes (Wikipedia Current Events: October 30–November 1, 2026). In Spain, modern high-speed rail engineering suffered a catastrophic failure as two high-speed passenger trains collided in Toledo province, leaving at least 69 dead and 179 wounded. Across Germany, protests and rioting erupted across 34 major cities—with looting in Frankfurt and clashes in Berlin—over energy inflation, while Portuguese riot police dismantled housing protest camps in Lisbon, and a private Learjet crash in Greenacres, Florida claimed nine lives.

To the secular observer, it looks like civilization's most sophisticated systems are fraying all at once.

Yet when you view these headlines through the unchanging lens of Scripture, you are confronted with a grounding, timeless truth: Not a single event from this past week caught the Sovereign Creator by surprise.

Here is what shook the world over the past seven days—and why our focus belongs firmly on the King of Kings.

1. The $6.3B Binance Cyberheist and the Illusion of Digital Treasure

On Friday, cryptocurrency exchange Binance confirmed that sophisticated state-sponsored actors bypassed digital vaults and purloined $6.3 billion in digital assets—the single largest heist in recorded human history (Wikipedia Current Events: October 30–November 1, 2026). Simultaneously, the Bank of Canada was forced to hike interest rates due to energy-driven inflation from the ongoing Persian Gulf tanker crisis.

Modern man believed he had finally invented invulnerable wealth: lines of encrypted code, decentralized ledgers, and digital balances untethered from physical reality. Yet in a matter of seconds, billions evaporated with a few keystrokes.

King Solomon diagnosed this exact folly three thousand years ago in Proverbs 23:5:

"When your eyes fly to it, it is gone, for suddenly it sprouts wings, flying like an eagle toward heaven."

And Christ gave us the eternal antidote in the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 6:19–20):

"Do not lay up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy and where thieves break in and steal, but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven... For where your treasure is, there your heart will be also."

Whether wealth is held in gold coins, paper dollars, or encrypted digital tokens, earthly treasure is vulnerable. A man who anchors his identity and peace in balance sheets will always live on edge.

Steward your household resources faithfully, eliminate foolish debt, work hard with your hands, but never confuse a financial portfolio with your ultimate security. Our Father in heaven knows what you need, and His kingdom can never be hacked or depleted.

2. The Toledo High-Speed Rail Disaster, the Florida Jet Crash, and the Vapor of Life

On Wednesday, October 28, two modern high-speed trains carrying 544 passengers collided near Los Yébenes in Spain, killing at least 69 people and injuring 179 (Wikipedia Current Events: October 28, 2026). Days later, a private Learjet 60 bound for the Bahamas crashed into a Florida neighborhood, killing all nine people aboard.

High-speed rail and private aviation represent the pinnacle of modern engineering and safety protocols. The people boarding that train in Spain and that jet in Florida had schedules, business meetings, family dinners, and weekend plans. They assumed safety was guaranteed.

Scripture gives us unvarnished truth in James 4:14:

"Yet you do not know what tomorrow will bring. What is your life? For you are a mist that appears for a little time and then vanishes."

And the Psalmist prayed in Psalm 90:12:

"So teach us to number our days that we may get a heart of wisdom."

You are not guaranteed seventy years, and you are not guaranteed tomorrow morning.

Do not waste this week holding petty grudges against family members, stewing in workplace resentment, or giving your children your exhausted leftovers while staring at a smartphone screen. Look your wife in the eyes tonight. Pray over your children before bed. Tell the people you love that you cherish them. Live with eternal intentionality.

3. Civil Unrest Across 34 German Cities and European Riots: The Breakdown of Human Institutions

Over the weekend, mass demonstrations against energy inflation and the cost of living escalated into violent clashes across 34 cities in Germany—including riots, looting, and street fires in Frankfurt, Berlin, and Cologne (Wikipedia Current Events: October 31, 2026). Riots broke out in Zurich, youth clashes erupted in The Hague, and Italian labor unions staged a nationwide general strike.

When the cost of energy spikes, food becomes expensive, and the promises of governments fail to deliver prosperity, civil unrest inevitably boils over. When a society detaches itself from God and puts its faith in government welfare and central planning, people panic when those systems shake.

Our grandfathers understood a foundational truth that modern culture has largely forgotten: true peace and stability are not gifts bestowed by governments. They are built from the bottom up by families who fear God, work hard, live within their means, and love their neighbors.

Paul wrote to believers navigating a tense, volatile Roman empire with clear instructions in 1 Thessalonians 4:11–12:

"Aspire to live quietly, and to mind your own affairs, and to work with your hands, as we instructed you, so that you may walk properly before outsiders and be dependent on no one."

Refuse to get swept into cultural anger, street panic, or political outrage. Be the steady hand, the calm neighbor, and the peaceful anchor in your community.

4. The Shift: Moving From Panic to Purpose

When you scan the headlines of train collisions, $6 billion cyberheists, and street riots across Europe, it is easy to feel a sense of helplessness.

Cynicism is the coward's way out. God did not place you in November 2026 by accident. He placed you in this exact generation to be an unshakeable pillar of light, quiet strength, and steady faith for your household and community.

Here is your battle plan for the week ahead:

Be the spiritual anchor of your home: Do not let your family hear you whining about cultural chaos. Open your Bible at the table, lead them in prayer, and remind them that God sits enthroned over history.

Be the steady hand at work: In your warehouse, job site, office, or shop, refuse to join in the chorus of fear, gossip, and complaint. Work with diligence and integrity.

Steward your local post: You cannot prevent hackers from draining crypto exchanges or stop train accidents in Europe. But you can do honest work, care for your wife, mentor a younger man, and serve your local church. Focus on what God placed directly before your hands.

Rest in the Unshakeable Kingdom: Empires will fall. Digital assets will vanish. Human institutions will crack. But our God reigns forever.

"Therefore let us be grateful for receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, and thus let us offer to God acceptable worship, with reverence and awe." — Hebrews 12:28

Step into this new week with your boots laced, your head held high, your household protected, and your faith anchored firmly in the Living God.

For Trump and America, a Clear Election Verdict Leaves a Murky Future https://t.co/KwVNJUdEp7
In the days since his defeat, President Trump has sounded like a man in denial.

With his party still picking through the wreckage of a political earthquake, a seemingly oblivious President Trump signed a steel beam for his new White House ballroom and flew to Florida to give a speech on the space program. He seems flat these days, maybe a little dazed.

If Donald Trump is still processing the election that swept his party from power in Congress last week, so too is Donald Trump’s America. Both parties are still absorbing the stunning reality of sweeping Democratic victories in states like Texas, Kansas and South Carolina that were long G.O.P. strongholds — and possibly even Mississippi.

But as clear as the midterm verdict was, the future is cloudier. After a decade in which Mr. Trump has dominated national politics, the country now faces a period of profound uncertainty, an interregnum between the time that Americans effectively decided that they were done with Mr. Trump and the time when he is actually done.

How does an unpopular, lame-duck president spurned by the electorate govern in his final two years in office? How does a shattered Republican Party rebuild itself for a post-Trump era while Mr. Trump himself is still around and unwilling to cede the stage? How do newly empowered Democrats use their new majorities in Congress and define themselves beyond simply being the anti-Trump party?

To those who wondered whether Mr. Trump would choose conciliation or confrontation in response to his party’s defeat, his decision on Friday to install Stephen Miller, his top ideological warrior, as the next White House chief of staff provided an answer — and it was not conciliation. In case the message was not received, on Saturday he posted an offer on social media for Dana White, the Ultimate Fighting Championship chief executive, to be his press secretary. Mr. Trump may be wounded, but a wounded animal can thrash around powerfully.

Yet those in his circle wasted no time looking past him. Two senior members of his team, Vice President JD Vance and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, quickly went public with sharply divergent views of the Iran war and the wisdom of prosecuting it. In effect, they began to set the parameters for a debate that will consume their party for the next year.

On Capitol Hill, evangelical Zionist Speaker Mike Johnson promptly indicated that he would step down, opening a leadership contest for the vanquished Republicans. And Democrats began mapping a path forward balancing the desire to investigate and hold Mr. Trump’s team accountable with the imperative of passing legislation addressing voter concerns about the cost of living.

One thing seems certain — the days of virtual one-man rule are over. In the nearly 22 months since Mr. Trump took office again, he has sought to impose his will not just over the executive branch but also over big business, the tech industry, major universities, law firms, the central bank, private banks, entertainment, sports, museums, the news media, national parks, the financial sector, the energy sector, the military and nonprofit foundations.

He has turned the prosecutorial power of the F.B.I. and Justice Department against his adversaries and, while he has been blocked at times by judges and grand juries, the Supreme Court has validated many of his assertions of authority. He has sent the National Guard into the streets of Washington and other cities, while turning ICE into a paramilitary force to haul away not just criminals but also otherwise law-abiding undocumented immigrants with deep roots in their communities. He has even sought to remake the face of Washington, tearing down the East Wing of the White House to make room for his new ballroom-qua-drone-launcher, building a helipad on the South Lawn, proposing a new triumphal arch, renovating the Reflecting Pool, etc.

Solomon, also Salomon (Hungarian: Salamon; 1053–1087) was King of Hungary from 1063. Being the elder son of Andrew I, he was crowned king in his father's lifetime in 1057 or 1058. However, he was forced to flee from Hungary after his uncle, Béla I, dethroned Andrew in 1060. Assisted by German troops, Solomon returned and was again crowned king in 1063. On this occasion he married Judith, sister of Henry IV, Holy Roman Emperor. In the following year he reached an agreement with his cousins, the three sons of Béla I. Géza, Ladislaus and Lampert acknowledged Solomon's rule, but in exchange received one-third of the kingdom as a separate duchy.

In the following years, Solomon and his cousins jointly fought against the Czechs, the Cumans and other enemies of the kingdom. Their relationship deteriorated in the early 1070s and Géza rebelled against him. Solomon could only maintain his rule in a small zone along the western frontiers of Hungary after his defeat in the Battle of Mogyoród on 14 March 1074. He officially abdicated in 1081, but was arrested for conspiring against Géza's brother and successor, Ladislaus.

Solomon was set free during the canonization process of the first king of Hungary, Stephen I, in 1083. In an attempt to regain his crown, Solomon allied with the Pechenegs, but King Ladislaus defeated their invading troops. According to a nearly contemporaneous source, Solomon died on a plundering raid in the Byzantine Empire. Later legends say that he survived and died as a saintly hermit in Pula (Croatia).

Early life
Solomon was a son of King Andrew I of Hungary and his wife, Anastasia of Kiev.[1] His parents were married in about 1038.[2] He was born in 1053[3] as his parents' second child and eldest son.[4]

His father had him crowned king in 1057 or 1058.[4][5] Solomon's coronation was a fundamental condition of his engagement to Judith, a sister of King Henry IV of Germany.[4][6] Their engagement put an end to the more than ten-year-long period of armed conflicts between Hungary and the Holy Roman Empire.[4][7][8] However, Solomon's coronation provoked his uncle, Béla, who had until that time held a strong claim to succeed his brother Andrew according to the traditional principle of seniority.[5][6][8] Béla had, since around 1048, administered the so-called ducatus or duchy, which encompassed one-third of the kingdom.[9]

According to the Hungarian Illuminated Chronicle, a 14th-century chronicle:

Because carnal love and ties of blood are wont to prove a hindrance to truthfulness, in King Andreas love for his son overcame justice, so that he broke the treaty of his promise, which in kings should not be; in the twelfth year of his reign, when he was worn out with age, he caused his son Salomon, who was still a child of five years, to be anointed and crowned king over all Hungary. He pretended that he did this to prevent injury to his kingdom, for the Emperor would not have given his daughter to his son Salomon unless he had crowned him. When therefore they sang at Salomon's coronation: "Be lord over thy brethren," and it was told to Duke Bela by an interpreter that the infant Salomon had been made king over him, he was greatly angered.[10]

According to the Illuminated Chronicle, in order to secure Solomon's succession, his father arranged a meeting with Duke Béla at the royal manor in Tiszavárkony.[6][7] The king proposed that his brother choose between a crown and a sword (which were the symbols of royal and ducal power, respectively), but had previously commanded his men to murder the duke if Béla picked the crown.[6][7]

The duke, whom a courtier had informed of the king's plan, chose the sword, then left Hungary after the meeting.[6][7] He sought the assistance of Duke Boleslaus the Bold of Poland and returned with Polish reinforcements.[5][8] Béla emerged the victor in the ensuing civil war, during which Solomon's father was mortally injured in a battle.[8] Solomon and his mother fled to the Holy Roman Empire and settled in Melk in Austria.[4][8][11]

Béla was crowned king on 6 December 1060,[5] but the young German king's advisors, who were staunch supporters of Solomon (the fiancé of their monarch's sister), refused to conclude a peace treaty with him.[12] In the summer of 1063, the assembly of the German princes decided to invade Hungary in order to restore Solomon.[13] Solomon's uncle died in an accident on 11 September, before the imperial army arrived.[14] His three sons—Géza, Ladislaus and Lampert—left for Poland.[11]

Suleiman I[a] (6 November 1494 – 6 September 1566), commonly known as Suleiman the Magnificent, was the Ottoman sultan from 1520 to 1566.[4]: 541–545  The longest reign among the Ottoman sultans, his rule brought about a notable peak in the Ottoman Empire's economic, military and political power, and raised the number of the empire's subjects to at least 25 million people.

After succeeding his father Selim I on 30 September 1520, Suleiman began his reign by launching military campaigns against the Christian powers of Central and Eastern Europe and the Mediterranean; Belgrade fell to him in 1521 and Rhodes in 1522, and at Mohács in 1526, Suleiman broke the strength of the Kingdom of Hungary. Hungary was subsequently divided, with much of it incorporated directly into the empire. However, his defeat at the siege of Vienna in 1529 prevented him from advancing further into Europe. Suleiman also fought for years against the Shia Islamic Safavid Empire of Iran and annexed Iraq. In North Africa, Ottoman Tripolitania was established and the Ottoman fleet dominated the seas from the Mediterranean to the Red Sea and into the Persian Gulf.[7]: 61 

Suleiman personally instituted major judicial changes pertaining to society, education, taxation, and criminal law. His reforms, carried out in conjunction with the Ottoman chief judicial official Ebussuud Efendi, brought together the two forms of Ottoman law: sultanic (Kanun) and Islamic (Sharia).[8] He was also a distinguished poet and goldsmith; and a great patron of fine culture, overseeing the "Golden Age" of the Ottoman Empire which was at the height of its artistic, literary, and architectural development.[9]

In 1534, Suleiman broke with Ottoman tradition by marrying Hürrem, an influential woman from his Imperial Harem who helped usher in the "Sultanate of Women" period in Ottoman history. Upon Suleiman's death in 1566, he was succeeded by his and Hürrem's son Selim II. The death of Suleiman marks a watershed moment in Ottoman history, although scholars typically regard the period after his death to be one of crisis and adaptation rather than of simple decline.[10][11][12] In the following decades, the Ottoman Empire began to experience significant political, institutional, and economic changes, a period often referred to as the Era of Transformation.[13]: 11 [14]

Synagogue of Satan (Greek: συναγωγή τοῦ Σατανᾶ, romanized: synagōgḗ toũ Satanã) is a phrase from Revelation 2:9 and 3:9 in which Jesus refers to a group persecuting the church, falsely claiming to be Jews. The exact meaning of who the text is referring to is unclear, but there are two prevailing views: either unbelieving Jews who did not recognize Jesus as a Messiah, or Christians who have integrated into practices of the surrounding culture. While it can be antisemitic if taken out of context, John of Patmos, the author of Revelation was likely Jewish and the use of the word "Jew" in Revelation is consistently positive.

Later Church Fathers used the same phrase or similar in polemical writings warning against Jews infiltrating the church, or Christians attending synagogue. During the Reformation, the phrase was used in polemics against the Catholic Church. The Catholic Church instead used the phrase as a descriptor of both the enemies of the church and Freemasonry.

In the modern era, the verses have been used to justify antisemitism by conspiracy theorists and followers of Christian Identity who believe the Serpent seed doctrine that Jews are the literal descendants of Satan. It is also used more generally as a pejorative of any non-Christian religious practices considered to be associated with idolatry or the devil.

Origin in Revelation
In the New Testament book of Revelation, in the letters to the early Christian churches of Smyrna and Philadelphia in Revelation 2:9 and 3:9, the author quotes Jesus as speaking of the Synagogue of Satan, in each case referring to a group persecuting the church "who say they are Jews and are not".[1]

And to the angel of the church in Smyrna write: "The words of the first and the last, who died and came to life. I know your tribulation and your poverty (but you are rich) and the slander of those who say that they are Jews and are not, but are a synagogue of Satan."

— Revelation 2:8–9 (ESV)
And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write... "I know your works. Behold, I have set before you an open door, which no one is able to shut. I know that you have but little power, and yet you have kept my word and have not denied my name. Behold, I will make those of the synagogue of Satan who say that they are Jews and are not, but lie—behold, I will make them come and bow down before your feet, and they will learn that I have loved you."

— Revelation 3:7–9 (ESV)
While the phrase "synagogue of Satan" is a negative term, the precise meaning in the text is uncertain. The association of Jews with Satan begins not in Revelation, but in the Gospel of John.[2] In John 8:44, Jesus charges the Jewish authorities as being of the devil.[3] Biblical scholar Stefan Schreiber draws parallels from this passage, Rev 2:9, 3:9, and Acts: "The devil as the opponent per se functions as a paradigm of the opposing Jewish majority refusing to accept Christ; so in John 8:44, the Jewish authorities are charged with having the devil as their father, and in Rev 2:9, 3:9, the Jewish communities in Asia Minor are dismissed as 'synagogue of Satan'. An opponent of the Christian mission from outside is called 'son of the devil' in Acts 13:10".[4]

There are two prevailing views of who is being referred to in this passage. The dominant view that it refers to unbelieving Jews, or those Jews who do not recognize Christ as Messiah.[5][6] The Oxford Handbook of the Book of Revelation summarizes this as "hostile ethnic Jews... no longer belong to the true community of God, the in-group, but to the 'synagogue of Satan,' the out-group. Thus, the true people of God are no longer 'those who say that they are Jews' but those who worship the almighty God as revealed in the Lamb that was slain".[7] New Testament scholar James Resseguie points out that according to the argument of various scholars supporting this view, Jews and Christians are locked in intense conflict in the regions to which the letters are addressed, and since Jews do not follow the Lamb, they belong, according to the author of Revelation, to the congregation of Satan.[8]: 88–89 

The alternative view is that this phrasing refers to heretical Christians following other doctrines such as the Nicolaitans or Jezebel.[5][6] Resseguie describes them as Christians who have integrated into the practices of the surrounding culture, pointing out that while the phrasing may seem antisemitic if taken out of context, the author of Revelation is likely Jewish and use of the word "Jew" in the book is consistently positive.[8]: 89 

Qumran community
Language similar to the "synagogue of Satan" phrasing in Revelation appears in the Dead Sea Scrolls, written by the Qumran community that viewed the rest of Judaism as apostate, calling its persecutors "the lot of Belial" (Satan).[9] The Community Rule uses "the lot of Belial" as a contrast to righteous community members. Through sin, humans place themselves in with Belial's lot.[10] This presents a cosmic dualism in which humans are either part of the light or part of the darkness, the lot of God or the lot of Belial.[11]

Post-Nicene polemics
During the Post-Nicene period, the exact phrasing from Revelation as well as similarly themed versions of it were used in various adversus judaeos (against the Jews) polemical writings addressing ongoing conflicts between Christians and Jews. While Jerome was the only Early Church Father to use the exact term "synagogue of Satan" as a pejorative,[12] other Post-Nicene Fathers such as Ambrose of Milan and John Chrysostom wrote on similarly phrased themes.

Jerome
Jerome used the "synagogue of Satan" phrasing as a polemic in his correspondence with Augustine of Hippo.[13]

If, however, there is for us no alternative but to receive the Jews into the Church, along with the usages prescribed by their law; if, in short, it shall be declared lawful for them to continue in the Churches of Christ what they have been accustomed to practise in the synagogues of Satan, I will tell you my opinion of the matter: they will not become Christians, but they will make us Jews.

— Jerome, Letters of St. Augustine, LXXV
Jerome also used the phrase in his letter to Pammachius and Oceanus, arguing that the Jews "persecute our Lord Jesus Christ in the synagogues of Satan".[14] Additionally, he used the similar phrase "synagogue of antichrist" in his polemical writing.[12]

Augustine
In addition to the uses by Jerome, the phrase was used by Augustine in at least one clear related usage. In On Baptism, Augustine engages a statement from the African bishop Rogatianus of Nova: "Christ established the Church, the devil heresy: how can the synagogue of Satan have the baptism of Christ?"[14]

I couldn’t access Nikkei’s full article, so this summarizes its available headline and description.

4.  Quanta Magazine: Researchers testing whether AI models can recognize their own internal activity found that some can detect artificially injected changes in their neural networks, suggesting a limited capacity for self-monitoring. In an initial Anthropic experiment, a powerful Claude model correctly detected and described injected concepts in about 20% of trials. Follow-up studies, however, indicated that describing those concepts could result from the manipulation itself, while detecting unusual internal activity remained harder to explain. Scientists disagree over whether this qualifies as introspection, and the findings do not establish consciousness or subjective experience, but they offer new ways to investigate AI processing and potentially human cognition.

5. Washington Post: Republicans’ heavy midterm losses have emboldened potential challengers to Vice President JD Vance for the 2028 presidential nomination, according to The Washington Post. Ron DeSantis, Brian Kemp and Ted Cruz are considering bids or preparations. Record partner turnover and aggressive recruitment are putting pressure on the traditional partnership model and threatening longstanding New York law firms.

The Joint List reportedly will not vote for the government but will also refrain from acting to bring it down.

The strikes damaged substations linking nuclear power plants to Kyiv and central Ukraine, along with facilities in several other regions. OUCH! KAMALA HARRIS FINISHES 16TH IN A 2028 DEMOCRATIC PRESIDENTIAL STRAW POLL — RECEIVING JUST SIX VOTES:

Former Vice President Kamala Harris received a disappointing result at the Crooked Con progressive gathering, finishing tied for 16th place in an informal straw poll of potential 2028 Democratic presidential candidates.

And the numbers are striking.

Out of 990 votes cast, Harris received just SIX.

That's 0.6% of the vote for the woman who was the Democratic Party's presidential nominee in 2024.

Meanwhile, Georgia Senator Jon Ossoff finished far ahead of the field with 38.4%.

Think about that for a moment.

Just two years ago, Kamala Harris was leading the Democratic presidential ticket, receiving national attention, fundraising support, and the backing of many of the party's biggest political figures.

Now, at this gathering of progressive activists, she barely registered.

SIX VOTES. OUT OF 990.

That's certainly not the kind of result a former presidential nominee would want to see while considering another run for the White House.

The numbers also raise questions about where progressive activists want to take the Democratic Party heading into 2028.

Do they want a familiar candidate with national experience? Are they looking for a new generation of leadership? Or are they seeking a different ideological direction altogether?

This particular straw poll cannot answer those questions for the entire Democratic electorate. It represents the preferences of attendees at one political event, not a scientific national survey.

But it does offer an interesting snapshot of how Harris performed among this group of politically engaged progressives.

And for someone who previously occupied the second-highest office in the country, finishing behind so many other potential candidates is noteworthy.

FROM THE WHITE HOUSE TO SIX VOTES IN A PROGRESSIVE STRAW POLL.

That's quite a political contrast.

With the 2028 presidential race approaching, the Democratic Party has plenty of decisions ahead about its leadership, messaging, and political priorities.

And if this result is any indication of sentiment among these particular activists, Kamala Harris has substantial work to do to rebuild enthusiasm within that audience.

HERE'S THE BIG QUESTION:

Do you think Kamala Harris will actually run for president again in 2028, or has her moment in national politics passed?

Taraji P. Henson asked for $500,000 to play Brad Pitt's mother. She got $150,000 and says about $30,000 of it was left. The movie made $335 million.  In the video below, Gayle King asks if she's quitting acting. Taraji covers her face and cries before she can say a word. Then she does the math out loud.  In 2008 she was third on the call sheet for The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, behind Pitt and Cate Blanchett. Her 2016 memoir says she'd been promised "somewhere in the mid six figures." At a 2023 SAG-AFTRA event she said she asked for $500,000 and was first offered $100,000.  It came up to $150,000 with a condition. She had to cover three months of New Orleans hotel bills herself. "Insult, meet injury," she wrote.  On The Real she did the sum. Half the $150,000 went to taxes. Her team took 30% of the full fee, $45,000. That left $30,000, and her son's school tuition that year was $30,000. "Literally, for five months, that's what I made."  The memoir puts her pay at less than 2% of what the studio paid the top name on that call sheet, Pitt.  She got an Oscar nomination for the role. Fifteen years later she said she almost walked away from The Color Purple over pay. That same month she told Gayle King: "Every time I do something and I break another glass ceiling, when it's time to renegotiate, I'm at the bottom again."  The case for the studio: Pitt sold the tickets, and she doesn't dispute his money. "They deserve to earn what they get," she said of Pitt and Blanchett.  Her side: "I too worked my ass off, and at the time I couldn't say no. I didn't have any power."  $335 million at the box office. An Oscar nomination. One year of school fees.  Every day, one star's real paycheck.  Was that Hollywood paying for box office power, or paying a Black woman less because it could?

text:
I AM NOT OVER THE IMMACULATE INCOMPLETION. 🏈

Fourth and 6. Down 31 to 24. Three and a half minutes left. Darian Mensah throws it to Elija Lofton in the end zone. Two hands on the ball. Two feet inbounds. Touchdown.

Incomplete.

Replay looked at it and said, yep, still incomplete. Mario Cristobal asked for an explanation and got, in his words, "Zero explanation. Zero."

Catholics vs. Convicts is back, and I am starting to think the Catholics might be the convicts.

Because I have seen this movie before. In 1988, Miami walked into Notre Dame Stadium ranked No. 1 and undefeated. Down 31 to 24 on fourth down in the fourth quarter, Cleveland Gary reached for the goal line and got ruled a fumble. On Saturday, Miami walked into Notre Dame Stadium ranked No. 1 and undefeated. Down 31 to 24 on fourth down in the fourth quarter, Lofton caught a touchdown and got ruled incomplete. Notre Dame scored 31 both times.

Same building. Same score. Same down. Same outcome. Thirty eight years apart.

(Yes, I know Andre Brown's touchdown in that 1988 game was not a catch either. I am a fan, not a judge.)

And here is my favorite part. The officiating crew was ACC. Our own conference did this to us. That is like getting mugged by your own family at Thanksgiving.

My proposed punishment is reasonable. Every official on that crew gets pantsed at midfield and then has to run a lap through Coral Gables. At noon. In November. We will provide sunscreen.

Now, as a Catholic, I hate to even ask this. But we have an American pope for the first time in history. He is from Chicago. South Bend is about ninety miles away. Did Leo have something to do with this? Were indulgences offered to the officiating crew? Did the replay booth get a plenary? I am just asking questions. Father, forgive me.

Here is the thing, though. Last year Miami lost to SMU in overtime in November and everybody said the season was over. Then the Canes went out and beat Texas A&M, beat Ohio State, beat Ole Miss, and played for a national title.

So the season is not over. One bad call does not end a year. It just ends my faith in replay.

But my God. That is the worst call against my team I have seen in a long, long time.

Go Canes. 🦋

text:
THE HISTORICAL BACKGROUND OF "SADZA"

Sadza (or isitshwala in Ndebele) is a stiff, thick porridge that has long been the central staple food for the indigenous peoples of Zimbabwe (primarily the Shona and related groups), eaten with a relish of vegetables, meat, or other sauces. The name and the dish form itself are indigenous, but the dominant modern version made from white maize meal is a post-contact development.

Pre-colonial foundations (small grains)
In the pre-colonial period, sadza was made from indigenous African “small grains”—primarily finger millet (known as zviyo, rapoko, rukweza, or njera), pearl/bulrush millet (mhunga), and sorghum (mapfunde). These were ground into flour (or meal) and cooked into a thick paste or stiff porridge that formed the main dish of the Shona and other groups in Zimbabwe.

Historians such as David Beach note that the Shona had cultivated these traditional grain crops for nearly 2,000 years before colonialism. They underpinned food security, the pre-colonial economy, and social life among  Karanga communities associated with states such as Great Zimbabwe, Torwa, Mutapa, and Rozvi.

The grains were versatile: ground for sadza/porridge, used for unleavened bread or cakes, cooked like rice in some preparations, and especially important for brewing opaque traditional beer (doro or hwahwa). They also supported livestock feed, building materials (stalks for granaries), and compost.

Finger millet in particular is often highlighted in sources as the classic pre-maize base (sadza rezviyo), producing a darker, stronger-flavored version that is still prepared today.

Small grains were relatively drought-tolerant and suited the environment, contributing to the reputation of productive African agriculture noted by early European observers.

These crops were central to a mixed farming-herding economy. Meals were typically communal, with sadza and relish shared from common bowls, reflecting social values of togetherness. The dish was (and remains) eaten by hand, often rolled into balls and dipped into the accompanying stew or greens.

Transition with maize
Maize (corn), a New World crop, reached Africa after 1500 as part of the Columbian Exchange, spreading via Portuguese and other coastal trade networks. Exact timing for the Zimbabwe is debated, some accounts place limited introduction or presence by the 16th–18th centuries, while others emphasize that it was not a major staple until the late 19th or early 20th century (around or after the Pioneer Column in 1890).

Maize offered higher yields under certain conditions and was promoted under colonial agriculture. It gradually displaced small grains as the primary source for sadza among many communities, especially in the 20th century, though millet and sorghum persisted longer in some areas for taste, beer-making, nutrition, and resilience during hardship. 
White maize meal became preferred; yellow maize was a fallback in shortages (sometimes nicknamed “Kenya”).

Continuity and cultural role
Even after the shift to maize, the form of sadza—the stiff porridge as the indispensable base of the meal—remained continuous from the pre-colonial era. It is still described as essential (“a meal is not a meal without sadza”), central to family and communal eating, and a marker of cultural identity. 

Traditional small-grain versions continue to be valued for their flavor, nutritional profile, and heritage, and small grains retained economic and social importance well into the colonial period.

The historical background of sadza lies in ancient African grain porridges of the Shona and related peoples. Maize transformed the ingredient but not the fundamental role of the dish as the staple that has sustained indigenous Zimbabwean communities for centuries.

text:
Patti Adkins (born May 4, 1972) was a 29-year-old single mother and assembly-line supervisor at the Honda of America plant in Marysville, Ohio. 

She was last seen just after midnight on June 29–30, 2001, when she clocked out at the end of second shift as the plant shut down for the July 4th week. 

She had arranged care for her 7-year-old daughter and boarded her pets, telling family and friends she was leaving for a secret week-long trip to a remote cabin in Canada with a married coworker she had been seeing on and off for years.

According to accounts from people close to her, the man had said he planned to leave his wife for her. She had given him roughly $90,000 (drawn from savings, 401(k) loans, and other sources) so he could buy out his share of a joint business with his wife. 

She was also told not to pack much and to hide under a tarp in the bed of his pickup so a coworker riding with them wouldn’t see her. 

She carried a small teal duffel bag (reportedly containing something from Victoria’s Secret). She never contacted anyone again and failed to pick up her daughter on July 8; her sister reported her missing. 

There has been no activity on her accounts or other signs of life since. 

She was later declared legally dead, and foul play is strongly suspected. Her body has never been found.

The man (whose name has never been publicly released by authorities) denied any romantic relationship or travel plans, claiming he barely knew her as a coworker. 

Police found items at his home that contradicted this, including gifts she had given him (such as a phone and T-shirt) and a letter from her. 

He failed a polygraph (showing deception), quit his job at the Honda plant shortly afterward and never returned, and gave an alibi involving a long wait at a Burger King drive-thru that the restaurant manager disputed. 

Cat hair from her pets and a tiny untestable blood spot were found on a truck-bed cover he had bought days earlier; cadaver dogs alerted on concrete he poured that week (it was dug up with no results). 

He remains the primary person of interest / suspect, but there has never been enough evidence for charges.

The overlay text on the billboard matches these publicly reported details exactly. 

The case is still open as a missing-person/homicide investigation with the Union County Sheriff’s Office; tips can go to them or Central Ohio Crime Stoppers (which has offered a reward). Coverage has continued into 2024–2025 as the case approaches the 25-year mark.

The photo on the billboard is a well-known image of Patti from around the time of her disappearance.

text:
***The Sabotage Nobody Explains and the Conversation Nobody Is Allowed to Have***

------
There are two things happening in Europe at the same time, and they reinforce each other. The first is a wave of sabotage and mysterious attacks for which an explanation is demanded, except that the explanation is never actually sought — only a culprit is assigned. The second is a taboo, increasingly enforced, on speaking with Vladimir Putin or with anyone whose ideas and actions we do not share. Together these two habits are dragging Italy into a confrontation with Russia that serves no Italian interest whatsoever.

Start with the sabotage. The number of suspected sabotage operations in Europe nearly quadrupled between 2023 and 2024, to more than thirty, according to the International Institute for Strategic Studies. When something blows up, the honest first question is the simplest one: who benefits? Would it be Russia? Ukraine? Or someone else entirely? This is not a provocative question, it is the elementary question of any serious investigation. Yet it is barely asked in public, because the answer has already been written before the inquiry begins. And once the culprit is fixed in advance, the facts stop mattering — what matters is whether you nod along. Anyone who raises the question is not treated as a sceptic but as an accomplice.

That is how the second taboo operates. Refusing to talk to Putin is presented as a virtue, as if diplomacy were a reward for good behaviour rather than an instrument for protecting your own country. It is the purest form of guilt by association: if you sit at the same table as someone, you must secretly agree with him. By that logic, no negotiation, no ceasefire, no arms control agreement would ever have been possible in the history of the world. You negotiate precisely with people you do not like, because those are the people with whom there is something to negotiate.

Jeffrey Sachs made this point plainly: real diplomacy means meeting all the parties involved in a conflict, and the European Union has done the opposite, refusing dialogue with Putin and with Lavrov. That is not toughness. It is a grave error, and Europe is paying for it. Sachs has spent around thirty years working on Russia, meeting in person the leaders in the Kremlin, in Washington and elsewhere, and reporting what he saw and heard. He is dismissed by people who have never crossed a border and who cannot get past the slogan that there is an aggressor and an aggrieved — as though a phrase learned by heart were the same thing as a history lesson.

The same quality was on display in the conversation with Sachs and Massimo D'Alema. Two men who would fit, many times over, into the space that current European leadership leaves empty. What they offer is not softness towards Moscow but a different intellectual instrument: the recognition that we are living in a multipolar world, that no single bloc can dictate its terms, and that in such a world the country that keeps talking is the country that keeps its options. When Sachs debated the new multipolar order for two hours with students in New York, the room was full and hungry for it. The young have already moved into that world. European officialdom has not.

So the question must be put bluntly, without embarrassment: why exactly is the European Union trying to wage war against Russia? Not to defend Ukraine, not to deter, not to negotiate from strength — but to wage it, as a project in itself. Italy has no quarrel with Russia. Italians did not choose this confrontation and will not gain from it. They will pay for it in energy, where in 2024 industrial electricity prices were 11% above the euro-area average, according to the Italian energy regulator. They will pay for it in industry, where Italian exports to Russia fell from 7.7 billion euros in 2021 to 4.3 billion in 2024. And they will pay for it in freedom of speech at home, where even artists and athletes are now expected to pass a loyalty test on whom they are allowed to admire.

Italy should want two things, and say them loudly. First, that every act of sabotage be investigated honestly, with the question of interest asked before the verdict. Second, that the telephone be picked up. Talking is not capitulation. It is what sovereign countries do when they refuse to be passengers in someone else's confrontation.

text:
WORLD NEWS TODAY
Sunday, November 8, 2026
Global Headlines | Politics | War | Economy | Science | Humanitarian Affairs
1. UNITED STATES — DEMOCRATS TAKE CONTROL OF CONGRESS
Democrats have won majorities in both chambers of Congress following the November 3 midterm elections, delivering a major setback to President Donald Trump.
Rising living costs, the war with Iran, healthcare, and public dissatisfaction shaped the election. Democrats are preparing investigations into the administration while promising action on affordability.
Trump remains president and retains veto power, setting up potential confrontations when the new Congress convenes in January.
Source: Associated Press, November 8.
2. IRAN — WAR CONTINUES AS DIPLOMACY FACES NEW TEST

The eight-month conflict involving the United States, Israel, and Iran remains a major international crisis.

President Trump said renewed American strikes were highly unlikely if negotiations produced a satisfactory agreement. Iran continues demanding sanctions relief and other concessions.

Maritime incidents near the Strait of Hormuz threaten global shipping. Iranian authorities reported tankers damaged by mines, while American forces reported disabling a vessel attempting to breach their blockade.

Some competing military accounts remain independently unverified.

Qatar continues mediating efforts to prevent further escalation.

Source: Reuters, November 8.

3. UKRAINE — NEW PEACE TALKS APPROACH

Ukraine, Russia, and the United States are preparing for negotiations in Abu Dhabi on November 10–11. France says European representatives will participate.

Meanwhile, Russian missile and drone attacks have damaged Ukrainian energy infrastructure, disrupting essential services as colder weather approaches.

Major disagreements remain over occupied territory, security guarantees, and Ukraine's future defense.

Diplomats see an opportunity for progress, but no comprehensive peace agreement has been finalized.

Source: Reuters, November 7–8.

4. ISRAEL — NETANYAHU FACES GOVERNMENT CHALLENGE

Israeli President Isaac Herzog has asked former military chief Gadi Eisenkot to attempt forming a government following the October 27 elections.

Neither Eisenkot nor Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secured a clear parliamentary majority.

Coalition negotiations could determine Israel's leadership and influence regional security, relations with Washington, and future policies toward Palestinians.

Eisenkot's appointment does not yet guarantee a change of government.

Source: Associated Press, November 8.

5. POLAND — KRAKOW MASS SHOOTING SHOCKS NATION

Poland has declared two days of national mourning following a shooting in Krakow's historic central square.

Six people were killed, and numerous others were wounded. Police also discovered three deceased family members at the suspected attacker's home.

Authorities are investigating possible far-right ideological influences, although the motive has not been conclusively established.

The tragedy has intensified debates about extremism, firearms, and public security.

Source: Reuters, November 8.

6. GLOBAL ECONOMY — ENERGY PRICES AND INFLATION PRESSURE HOUSEHOLDS

Disrupted Gulf shipping and continuing geopolitical uncertainty are placing pressure on energy markets.

In the United States, annual inflation has reached 3.7%, while federal debt-servicing costs exceed $1 trillion annually.

Economists warn that addressing household affordability while reducing government deficits will require difficult decisions.

Artificial intelligence investment offers opportunities for economic growth but raises concerns about employment displacement.

Source: Associated Press, November 8.

7. CLIMATE — COP31 NEGOTIATIONS BEGIN IN TURKEY

Nearly 200 countries are meeting in Antalya for COP31 climate negotiations.

Delegates are discussing emissions reductions, climate financing, adaptation, and implementation of existing commitments.

Singapore's environment minister warned that sweeping new targets are unlikely, emphasizing practical delivery of previous agreements.

Financing disagreements and competing national energy priorities remain major obstacles.

Source: Reuters, November 8.

8. JAPAN — EARTHQUAKE INJURES AT LEAST 22

A magnitude 5.5–5.7 earthquake struck central Japan early Sunday, damaging storefronts and injuring at least 22 people.

The earthquake originated beneath Shizuoka Prefecture, affecting surrounding regions.

Authorities warned of possible aftershocks and urged residents to remain prepared.

No unusual changes were initially reported along the Nankai Trough fault system.

Source: Associated Press, November 8.

9. AFRICA — MIGRANT TRAGEDY OFF SENEGAL

At least 21 people died after a migrant vessel sank off Senegal's coast, government officials reported.

The disaster underscores continuing dangers along Atlantic migration routes, where people risk dangerous sea crossings in search of security and economic opportunity.

Source: Reuters, November 8.

10. TECHNOLOGY — AI TRANSFORMS COMMERCE AND CYBERSECURITY

Artificial intelligence shopping assistants are emerging as potential competitors to conventional online search and retail advertising models.

Major retailers face uncertainty over how automated purchasing may reshape consumer behavior.

Separately, Japan has announced a roughly $63 million emergency cybersecurity initiative following attacks affecting businesses and government institutions.

Sources: Reuters, November 8; Associated Press, November 6.

WORLD OUTLOOK — WHAT COMES NEXT?

Three developments deserve particular attention: whether American-Iranian negotiations prevent renewed attacks, whether Ukraine peace discussions produce credible security arrangements, and how the incoming Democratic Congress confronts the Trump administration.

Climate negotiations, energy disruptions, economic pressures, and emerging technologies will also shape international decisions.

THE CENTRAL MESSAGE: The world faces serious challenges, but diplomacy, responsible leadership, scientific progress, and international cooperation remain essential paths toward greater stability.

WORLD NEWS TODAY — NOVEMBER 8, 2026

Reporting based on Reuters and Associated Press coverage available November 8, 2026. Developing events and preliminary figures remain subject to revision.

text:
😂🤣😂🤣😂🤣

Two facts that cut Tehran's language down to size:

**It was never Iran's to open.** The Strait of Hormuz is an international waterway — roughly 21 miles wide at its narrowest, with the shipping lanes running through both Iranian *and Omani* waters, and transit passage through it is a right under international law, not a favor Tehran grants. A country can't "reopen" a strait it doesn't own.

**And it never actually closed.** Shipping through Hormuz was attacked, harassed, and slowed during this war — traffic dropped hard at the worst points — but tankers kept transiting throughout. The only genuine *blockade* in effect in those waters is **America's** — the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports, which is one of the very things Tehran is demanding be lifted.

So strip Araghchi's offer down to what it really is: Iran is offering to **stop threatening the shipping it never had the right to stop**, in exchange for the U.S. lifting a blockade the U.S. actually controls, plus sanctions relief and frozen assets. "We will reopen the strait in two days" is Tehran selling Washington something that was never Tehran's — and framing its own restraint as a concession. I'll use it your way from here: not closed, and not Iran's to open.

After one recall petition and election against the same officer during a term, no further recall can be filed against that person for the remainder of the term.​
Ballotpedia
As of November 8, 2026, incumbent Gov. Tony Evers (term ending early January 2027) has long met the one-year requirement. Governor-elect David Crowley (elected November 3, 2026) will take office around January 4, 2027, and would not be subject to recall until after one year in office.​
Jsonline
Signature requirement
Valid signatures of qualified electors equal to at least 25% of the votes cast for the office of governor in the last preceding gubernatorial election, statewide (for the governor).​
law.justia
Based on the 2022 election (~2,656,490 total votes), this is roughly 664,123 valid signatures. The exact figure is determined by the filing officer using official canvass results. Once the 2026 election results are the “last preceding,” the threshold will update to 25% of those votes.​
Uselectionatlas
Basic steps
Register the effort: A qualified elector (U.S. citizen, 18+, resident of the relevant district for the required period) must file a campaign registration statement and a Statement of Intent to Circulate a Recall Petition with the proper filing officer before circulating any petitions. For statewide offices such as governor, this is typically the Wisconsin Elections Commission / Secretary of State office (the same officer who receives nomination papers). Circulating before proper registration invalidates signatures.​
law.justia
Circulate the petition:
Petitions must be clearly headed “RECALL PETITION.”
Circulation is limited to 60 days from the date of registration. The completed petition must be offered for filing by 5:00 p.m. on the 60th day.
Only signatures dated within that 60-day window count. Each sheet needs a completed Certification of Circulator.
Signers must be qualified electors of the relevant jurisdiction.​
Ballotpedia
File and verification: The petition is filed with the same officer. The officer reviews it for sufficiency. The targeted official has a short window to challenge; petitioners can rebut. If certified as sufficient, a recall election is ordered.​
law.justia
Recall election: Held on the Tuesday of the 6th week after the certificate of sufficiency (or the next non-holiday if needed). The incumbent continues in office until results are declared and is automatically a candidate unless they decline within 10 days. Other candidates may file as in a special election. For partisan offices, it generally functions as a regular election for the remainder of the term; a primary may apply in certain multi-candidate nonpartisan situations. The winner serves the rest of the term.​
law.justia
Practical notes
Requirements are strict on form, timing, registration, and circulator certifications. Errors (incomplete registration, signatures outside the window, missing certifications) commonly lead to invalidation.

Ballotpedia
This is a summary of the constitutional and statutory framework. For an actual effort, rely on official Wisconsin Elections Commission materials and legal advice, as procedural details and exact numbers can depend on the precise timing and certified results.

text:
There’s a version of the world where the US uses stablecoins to advance its policy objectives in AI.

A point made recently on @theallinpod was that AI companies are competing w/ the US gov for capital in the bond markets. This raises qs about where the gov will find marginal buyers for its debt and whether, as AI tests the boundaries of US power, it will feel compelled to intervene. Given the political developments of this past week, that possibility seems more likely.

Stablecoins could offer a tech forward way for the US to generate demand for its debt while asserting influence over the AI economy.

Tether is already one of the largest holders of US Treasuries. And the supply of stablecoins growing creates demand for US debt. Also, much of the demand for dollar stablecoins comes from outside the US, meaning pro stablecoin policy could channel foreign demand for dollars into US Treasuries.

There may also be a longer term benefit, though this is way more speculative. Digitally native intelligence may gravitate toward digitally native money. As AI agents become economic participants, their choice of currency becomes a matter of geopolitical importance.

By promoting dollar stablecoins, the US could position the dollar as the reserve currency of AI

h/t @alekslarsen for seeding the idea

text:
So, for those who might not be paying attention, I am not just an aging film school dropout who does silly meta AI cartoons, features about fat people and rants about how stupid Hollywood is.

I am actually a highly respected (if rarely listened to) and occasionally well-paid international media consultant. (See my post on consulting in Dubai.) Yes, you're right to be skeptical. I'm still skeptical about it. But it is legal. I checked.

About a year ago, at the beginning of this whole AI creator craze, I was approached by some startups looking to bring me aboard or pay me for advice. Having already worked on a few failed startups, I wasn't interested in joining another one. (Despite making some good dough along the way.) And it seemed unethical to charge them for advice they wouldn't listen to. (Though that rarely stopped me in the past.)

So I just offered my advice for free. It was:

"Don't. No. Stop. It won't work. And it's kind of sleazy that you're even thinking about it." (They didn't listen to me.)

Because the startup model they were interested in pursuing, which is just a variation on almost every startup model these days, was: get suckers to sign up with big dreams of success, take a cut of whatever their content earned, and try to lock them into subscriptions for bonus features (more like bugs).

As I've stated before, I don't see long-term prospects for companies built on trying to rip off indie creators. That was proven by MySpace decades ago. However, people keep trying, and sometimes can get a little quick revenue to try to expand before they fail. It's a sleazy business, trying to make a quick profit off hopes and dreams while offering little in return.

The general idea of a YouTube alternative is worthy. But, while trying not to call any specific companies out, I've seen few that strike me as both well-intentioned and potentially viable.

However, AethrFlix seems different.

Importantly, they have been wise enough never to ask for my advice. Statistically, that is a plus for the future success of any startup. (This post is not a paid promotion. I have no association with the company. And for their own protection, I do not officially endorse it.)

The person behind the site is Grimfel, someone I've followed for some time and respect. He's a strongly opinionated member of the AI music and video community, with plenty of experience creating his own work. And solid tech skills. That doesn't guarantee he can build a successful distribution platform, but understanding creators is a useful place to start.

What seems particularly promising is a key differentiator: a Blu-ray purchase and print-on-demand option that, if it works as advertised, could make getting a physical release remarkably painless.

Now, I don't think there's any real money in selling Blu-rays for most indie creators. At least not in the foreseeable future. But that's not really the point.

A few core fans might want to buy your film on disc. You want passionate fans to have that option. And it's great to have an easy way to buy a bunch yourself and hand them out to friends or sell in person. You want the film to look good, the package to look good, and the person ordering it to actually receive it. You don't want to become a part-time disc manufacturer and shipping department. Having all that handled smoothly is a genuine service. It likely won't make anyone rich but it's a real bonus.

And who knows. I've been hoping for a BlueRay rival on the scale of the vinyl record revival. With people getting tired of streaming subscriptions, and concern about films being censored or dropped for sale and streaming, owning a physical copy has an appeal of its own. Once you've got the disc, you don't have to wonder whether the film will still be in the catalog next month. It might be a market that will grow over the next few years, especially with new original, likely edgy, SI content.

Then, hopefully, you also make a few bucks from streaming. If the creator's share is good, a small audience that actually watches your film might be worth more than being buried on YouTube. Being available to millions of people isn't quite the same as millions of people watching.

Of course, the audience still has to show up. AethrFlix still has to demonstrate that the service works, the terms are reasonable, and creators get what they're promised. Good intentions and a good idea aren't the same as a viable business.

But there's a difference between promising filmmakers fame and fortune and offering them something useful at a realistic scale. The burden will always be on the creators to make stuff people value enough to support.

Not every useful business has to replace YouTube. Sometimes it just has to do a few things YouTube doesn't. That's why this one is something to check out and follow.

Still, they shouldn't ask for my advice. Let's not ruin it.
