text:
THE EVIDENCE™

HAVE WE COME FULL CIRCLE? AMERICA BUILT BETTER CAVES. THE BIBLE TELLS US HOW THAT ENDS.

The evidence will be presented. The verdict is yours.

We split the atom, put men on the moon, and built machines that can track a missile across a continent. Then we took nearly 700,000 tons of granite out of a Colorado mountain so that, if the weapons we invented ever came for us, the people directing our defense could do what human beings have done for thousands of years when danger closed in. Get inside the rock.

There is a passage in Revelation that ought to make anyone who puts his ultimate faith in a mountain stop and read it twice. It describes kings, rich men, and military commanders hiding in caves and among the rocks of the mountains. They are terrified. And the thing they want the mountain to hide them from is God Himself.

WE WENT BACK TO THE CAVE

D.U.M.B.s is shorthand for deep underground military bases. The documented examples are impressive enough. At Cheyenne Mountain, the U.S. Air Force describes a complex some 2,000 feet inside granite, protected by blast doors weighing up to 25 tons. NORAD uses the facility as an alternate operations center. A declassified military history documents Raven Rock’s role as an alternate command site. Congress had its own emergency relocation facility beneath the Greenbrier resort in West Virginia, kept secret for decades until reporter Ted Gup exposed it in 1992.

The military logic is sound. If an attack destroys a headquarters, somebody still has to assess the damage, warn the country, and direct the response. A bunker can buy time and keep people alive. The Bible describes a day when those same instincts send people underground, and all the rock above them gives them no peace at all.

THE MEN WHO HAD EVERYTHING WILL BE SHAKING

Revelation 6:15–17 names “the kings of the earth,” “the rich men,” and “the chief captains.” It also includes “every bondman, and every free man.” The passage puts people who can command armies and people who have no power at all in the same scene. They hide “in the dens and in the rocks of the mountains” and cry out:

“Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him that sitteth on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb: For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand?”
— Revelation 6:16–17, KJV
Read what they ask the mountain to do. They want it to fall on them. They have reached the point where being buried alive seems preferable to facing the One they have spent their lives avoiding. A man might have spent a fortune to get inside that mountain. In the end, he is begging for the mountain to come down on his head.

THE GOLD AND SILVER WILL FAIL THEM TOO

Ezekiel describes the terror of judgment on Jerusalem in physical terms. “All hands shall be feeble, and all knees shall be weak as water.” A few verses later, the people throw their silver into the streets. Imagine what has to happen before a man who has spent his life accumulating wealth looks down at his silver and decides it is worth more to him lying in the gutter than in his hands.

“They shall cast their silver in the streets, and their gold shall be removed: their silver and their gold shall not be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of the LORD.”
— Ezekiel 7:19, KJV

James presses the point further. In his warning to the rich who hoarded wealth and withheld workers’ wages, he writes, “Your gold and silver is cankered,” and says that “the rust of them shall be a witness against you” (James 5:3, KJV). The tarnished treasure becomes evidence. What they spent their lives piling up will testify about what they did to get it and what they refused to do with it.
THE VERDICT

Have we come full circle? We have returned to the oldest refuge we know. We have reinforced it with steel, run power and communications into it, and calculated how much punishment it can take. Those calculations can tell us whether a blast door will hold. Revelation asks what happens when the person behind that door can no longer bear the thought of facing God.

The most sobering detail is whose wrath they fear. It is the wrath of the Lamb. The same Jesus Christ they beg the mountain to hide them from is the One who offers them refuge now. A man can spend his whole life preparing for the day the world turns against him and never give a thought to the day he will stand before God.

There is still time to turn to Him. The men in the caves had waited until all they could do was beg the rocks to fall.

The evidence has been presented. The verdict is yours.

THE EVIDENCE™ | Kim Wojcinski — USA Best Selling Author

text:
Last winter, my coworker Kiyota spent one week in South Dakota and came home believing Americans give away land with every meal.

Nobody has corrected him.

Before the trip, our boss briefed him: "South Dakota is cattle country. A lot of people there own ranches."

Kiyota wrote it down. Ranch. Land. Cows. Very valuable.

First day. Lunch. A pizza place with his American coworker, Troy.

The waitress set down the pizza and asked:

"You want ranch with that?"

Kiyota froze.

In Japan, when a stranger offers you something enormous, you politely refuse.

"No, thank you. That is too much."

"Hon, it's free."

"...Free?"

"Always."

That night, he called me in Tokyo. He was whispering.

"They are giving away land at lunch."

Day two. Chicken wings.

"Ranch or blue cheese?"

Kiyota looked at Troy for help.

Troy said, "Ranch. Always ranch. Blue cheese people can't be trusted."

So in America, they make you choose between land and cheese. And it's a character test.

He chose the ranch.

A tiny plastic cup of white sauce arrived.

Kiyota studied it for a long time. He is an engineer. He decided it was symbolic. A deed you could dip.

He did not eat it. He put the lid back on and carried it to his hotel with both hands.

By Friday, there were fourteen cups in his mini-fridge.

He told me he owned fourteen ranches.

On the last night, at dinner, he finally asked Troy about it.

"I cannot believe they give it to everyone."

"That's South Dakota, man. Everybody gets ranch."

"Even children?"

"Especially children. Kids here start on ranch before they can walk."

Kiyota was moved. In Japan, a man works his whole life for a small apartment.

"My father worked fifty years. He never had one."

Troy put down his fork.

"Your dad's never had ranch?"

"Never."

"Bro." Troy looked genuinely upset. "We gotta fix that."

"I could bring one home to him?"

"Take a whole gallon, man. They sell it by the gallon at the store."

Kiyota wrote this down. In America, land is measured in gallons.

He was not surprised. This is the country that measures temperature in Fahrenheit.

"How many gallons does a family need?"

"Family of four? A gallon a week, easy."

"A week."

"Yeah. It goes fast."

"What do you grow on it?"

Troy squinted at him. "Grow? Nothing. You put it on stuff. Carrots. Celery. Pizza. Everything."

"You put the ranch... on top of the vegetables."

"Every time."

Kiyota sat back in his chair.

In Japan, the vegetables go on the land.

In South Dakota, the land goes on the vegetables.

"Do neighbors ever fight over it?"

"Oh, all the time. Store-bought versus homemade. My mom and my aunt haven't spoken since Easter."

Kiyota nodded slowly. "In Japan, too. Families fight over land."

"Man," Troy said. "We're not so different."

They shook hands. Both of them were very moved. Neither of them was talking about the same thing.

At the airport, Troy was waiting at the curb with a gift. A one-gallon jug of ranch. Red bow on top.

"For your dad."

Kiyota bowed so low his backpack slid over his head.

He checked the jug like a newborn. Wrapped in three sweaters.

Back in Japan, he drove straight to his parents' house. His father is 79. A rice farmer for fifty years.

Kiyota knelt and held out the jug with both hands.

"Father. I have brought you a ranch from South Dakota."

His father bowed and received it with both hands.

He opened it. He poured a little on a cucumber from his own field. He ate it.

A long silence.

"This," his father said, "is the best land I have ever eaten."

Kiyota found out what ranch was in March. From a YouTube video. He sat in his car for twenty minutes.

He has decided not to tell his father.

His father puts it on everything now. Rice. Tofu. Grilled fish. He tells the neighbors a young man in South Dakota gave him a ranch.

Troy says that's exactly what happened.

text:
Here's how things have been so far:

- I have no memory of January 
- February Spawn 2 graduated high school early
- March my friend in LA passed away
- No memory of April
- May was a lot of birthdays. Spawn 1 graduated high school, turned 18, & was accepted to uni all within the same week. I also helped catch a child predator that week.
- June I went to LA for my friend's memorial service
- July I moved Spawn 2 in with their grandparents bc kiddo wanted to help them out
- August was DEFCON, and the day I got back my stepfather passed. Spent most of August at my mom's handling his estate. School started for Spawn 3 at the same time. We spent almost $3,000 we didn't have to handle his affairs
- September I attempted and failed the PenTest+ but hey my sister finally got her disability approved after having a stroke 4yrs ago
- October started with my stepfather's memorial service in Alabama, and ended with my aunt passing away in Alabama. I spent almost this entire month in Alabama, spending money to help family manage final arrangements and financial transitions. I did get a job offer, but it's contingent on the approval of a clearance. Waiting phase.
- November began with my Alabama aunt's funeral and learning that my Louisiana aunt might have cancer in her lungs again. Waiting on further results and trying to get her a wig. Surgeries and chemo are tearing her up.

Y'all I'm like $15k in credit card debt bc nobody else in the family can do what I do. This is the longest I've been home in 6mos and I've only been home for 4 days.

I have until Dec 31 to pass PenTest+ and my brain is mush.

text:
You see this map is fascinating to me. It is so easy shout "#AI - Slop!!" at everything the machines help us to produce, but that is truly biased and foolish.

I could have prompted for the map generation from just an #MECFS word cloud, but what's fascinating to me is that... 🧵

...this map was generated after I'd spent 20 minutes explaining my entire treatment protocol and theory to the AI involved.

And you can see that it really has taken many of the ideas from the new protocol on board.

Let's look at one example:

The label "MECFS" is a forced and uncomfortable contradiction. In reality there remains a stark split between M.E and CFS. The true state of affairs remains a boxing ring where biomedical and psychological interpretations endlessly and fruitlessly duke it out.

New patients are almost immediately confronted with a false choice, one that will condemn them to a life of permanent illness: 

In one dogma you are permitted to focus on over-exertion, (PEM). In the opposing dogma you have to subscribe to the idea of under-exertion, (de-conditioning). Each philosophy rejects the other and in so doing dooms the patient.

The AI's map however, records a little area where both camps exist with equal priority. The AI immediately understood a concept that medicine and activism have singularly failed to comprehend: 

M.E is worsened by both under- and over-exertion.

Now, to be fair, I had to re-prompt it to ensure CBT and GET were added.  I specified them as unreachable islands... because that is what they are. They are unicorns, magical treatments that pretend to offer patients hope but when patients try to reach them, off the cliff edges they fall.

The Pace Trial is on twice. Yeah, well, so is Micro-timeshifting, it's an error, right? No, actually not. The Pace of "the Western Deserts" is a land of drought and suffering. It is a place where science goes to die and patients stagger in the dry heat of medical hubris and cruelty.

The other Pace Trial, well, that's a different fortification. It is built on firmer ground, there is utility in there, but it remains close, so close, to the endless mountains of fatiguability and the rocky treacherous shore.

Crash city is an inspired representation of the personal ruin of M.E. And PEM itself is presented as a citadel, fortified, protected even, by those who hold on to the defining characteristic of their illness - either because their identity now requires it, or because of the decades of unsubstantiated, unfounded denial and humiliation they have received while simply trying to report their primary symptom.

I like that Advocacy gets it's own tower and I like that recovery is represented in stone. I am so proud and pleased to see just how well those who have recovered have stood up for themselves and their lived experience against the barrage of ignorant hate.

I'd have added a wild, savage area of barbs and briars to stand for activism and for those who believe that they can cure M.E by force and strength of numbers and by bullying. Strategy, deceit, tribalism - these things played no part in my own recovery pathway, they were obstacles, boulders thrown. Recovery was more simply a job of work and a triumph of self-reliance and endurance.

And the largest city in The Realm of M.E is Fatigue itself. This is where #pwme spend most of their lives, in a holding pattern.

Little changes in M.E over decades and the daily grind of survival and defending oneself is the primary feature of the disease. It is the primary time sink. It is where your life goes.

I'd remove "The Baseline" as I don't believe in the concept, but then others do, so I can see why its on. I love the sea monsters representing the unknown and unknown dangers.

Unknown here is a literal thing, I don't consider it to be a proper diagnostic classification. The idea that you can define a useful condition based on medical unexplainably is rot. It is the ultimate waste-basket diagnosis given by a profession who wants to put M.E patients in the trash.

And my own work pops up - and of course I don't question the inclusion or the duplication of that!! Chronobiology, micro-timeshifting and orchestration; The activity curve. The keys that I believe will unlock M.E for all.

And so the AI did an absolutely remarkable job. It combined the important external concepts with what it had just learned about my new approach to the disease.

And it made it into a pretty chopping board map that I could actually laser cut and hang on the wall. Huh.

How did it do this? How did it exceed the capacity of both modern medicine and contemporary activism? The answer is very very simple.

It listened.

text:
If a person is afraid of dogs, they have the right to quickly try to get away — especially in the tight quarters of an elevator. It is not a justification for the dog running toward them, barking ferociously, and knocking into them. If the owner does not have control, that person is liable.
A dog owner is responsible for the dog’s behavior. Ferocious barking alone in a confined space is reason enough not to bring the dog — elevators offer nowhere to retreat, which is exactly why service and therapy dogs are specially trained and screened for calm dispositions. This dog is not that. A muzzle does not stop a large dog from knocking someone down.
People fear dogs for legitimate reasons: previous bites, childhood trauma, religious upbringing, or the danger itself. The CDC recorded eighty-one U.S. deaths from being bitten or struck by dogs in twenty twenty-one. Someone confronting a charging dog does not owe its owner a demonstration of composure. Retreat is a foreseeable response, especially in tight quarters.
The law recognizes that serious dog injuries do not require teeth. In Farrior versus Payton, women fell escaping a charging German shepherd without being bitten or touched; the court held the evidence warranted jury consideration. In Missouri in twenty twenty-one, a man settled for one hundred forty thousand dollars after retreating from a neighbor’s dog and breaking his hip without contact. A Stockton case settled for two hundred twenty-five thousand after a chained dog lunged, a man stepped backward, fell, and fractured his hip. In Pauszek versus Waylett, twenty nineteen, prior lunging and notice supported allowing a fright-induced fall claim to proceed. In Gloucester in twenty twenty-four, an escaped one-hundred-twenty-pound dog knocked down an elderly pedestrian, fracturing her hip and femur; the settlement was five hundred thousand dollars. An office-building parking garage case settled for one million after an unleashed dog caused a woman to strike her head on a brick wall.
Those settlements imposed financial consequences. Accuracy also requires acknowledging McGrellis versus Bromwell, twenty twenty: the owners won because foreseeability was not established. Responsibility must be proved, not assumed.
Criminal consequences exist too. California Penal Code section three ninety-nine addresses serious injuries caused by known mischievous animals allowed loose or kept without ordinary care. Maine’s twenty nineteen law makes leaving a qualifying dog assault without fulfilling aid and identification duties a crime.
Apply the personal test: if an uncontrolled dog charged your terrified parent, child, or spouse in an elevator and knocked them down, would you laugh — or look for a very good lawyer? The person’s religion is irrelevant to negligence. Mocking their fear does not excuse the owner’s failure to control the dog.
If you cannot control your dog, do not bring it where people are trapped with it.

Day 61 of writing ancient sales letters by hand to become a skilled copywriter.

I SWEAR THIS TIME IT'S REAL.

There is no video.

There is no singing of a Kanye West song.

And there is NO tooth fairy.

Much to my dismay. 

The advertisement we are covering today has two iterations. 

This one is the first among them.

It originally aired on the radio until they printed it in California. 

Twas for Rainier Ale - who were exclusively selling on the west coast at this time. 

They were located in Seattle, but they sponsored a San Francisco station. 

After the initial success of Howard Gossages radio ad, they decided to print it as well.

So, with this first iteration they chose somewhere further down the coast - where the broadcast also ran.

This one was humorous. 

The language was also rather intentional due to their target demographic of 'Scholars."

Really feels like they were after intellectuals, artists, and fashionistas.

Somewhere between Seattle and San Francisco is a city full of these people!

I'm sure they got around to that market.

This ad reads as brand awareness mixed with a separate offer. 

It's so funny to me...because...in middle school I remember sweatshirts that were very similar. 

Back in Oklahoma City, kids were wearing Benjamin Franklin shirts with his portrait. 

But instead of his name beneath it and a respectful image of the founding father...

...it was dollar signs on his eyes and several bands surrounding him - truly tasteful streetwear.

On a serious note, they always gave me a great laugh.

There is nothing wrong some Big Ben Drip.

Another thing this letter does well is come off as flippant regarding the service they do.

Like "it's not really a big deal man."

We wanted to give out these sweatshirts for free bro. 

BUT

"...state laws and our own prudence forbid it."

You're killing me smalls.

WHO IS FALLING FOR THIS!?

Obviously, people on the West Coast.

Ouch. 

I don't really despise California. 

Great place to visit!

Not to stay!

I did live there for five years but that was a long time ago. 

That aside, I implore you all to take a closer look at this ad by Howard Gossage.

Now...

…for those of you who are copy lovers, new and old...

Or maybe someone who wants to write more persuasive content?

To get more leads, sales, or even views?

I highly recommend two things!

1. Do the same as I, handwrite old sales letters and work on learning just as much as writing.

AND

2. Join @TheCopyTitan Svet Dimitrov's Skool for copywriting.

They are an extremely pleasant bunch, and I see it growing to become much larger in due time.

I really cannot recommend this guy enough.

If you’d like to see all the recorded masterclasses…

…as well as Svet's weekly copy breakdowns.

My affiliate link to his wonderful community is in my bio.

Please take a peek.

Alrighty then.

To end in similar fashion.

Please feel free to point out where I'm wrong…

…where I'm Mistaken…

OR

Perhaps even where I'm right.

Although I do learn the most in knowing what I did wrong.

Thank you for reading this!

text:
WHAT HAPPENS TO YOUR MONEY WHEN YOU SUBSCRIBE TO ANTHROPIC AS A VIP ON BITGET IPO PRIME?

I have already covered Anthropic's upcoming IPO through @Bitget IPO Prime in my previous posts regarding the differences between the VIP and Public subscription rounds.

This time, let us focus on Bitget VIP users, especially how their subscription works, how allocations are calculated, and what happens to the money that does not get allocated.

For example, what happens if you commit $100,000 but only receive a portion of that amount in IPO exposure?

@Bitget recently shared an infographic explaining the VIP subscription process using a hypothetical $100,000 commitment, so let me walk you through the numbers.

1️⃣ SUBSCRIPTION AND PRICING

An eligible VIP user commits $100,000 through IPO Prime and waits for the final IPO offering price to be determined.

During this period, the committed funds are locked and cannot be freely withdrawn or transferred.

2️⃣ ALLOCATION

Suppose the platform allocates 80% of the subscription.

That means $80,000 of the original $100,000 commitment would be allocated toward the IPO-linked asset.

However, this is just an example. Actual allocations depend on how many shares Bitget secures and the total subscription demand.

3️⃣ REFUNDS AND FEES

The remaining $20,000 would be the unallocated portion.

For the VIP Round, the underwriting service fee is 12% of the allocated amount, which would equal $9,600 in this example.

The fee is deducted from the unallocated balance, leaving an actual refund of $10,400.

So the amount returned to your account may be less than the unallocated portion once applicable fees are accounted for.

4️⃣ WHAT HAPPENS TO THE REFUNDED FUNDS?

Bitget also offers an IPO Prime Exclusive Earn benefit.

If the feature is enabled and the funds meet the applicable requirements, eligible refunded amounts can be automatically transferred into an Earn product offering up to 10% annualized APR for 15 days.

10% APR does not mean earning 10% in just 15 days. The actual interest is calculated based on the applicable annualized rate and subscription period.

5️⃣ WHEN DO YOU RECEIVE YOUR ALLOCATION?

For the VIP Round, the corresponding rANT tokens are expected to arrive within three to five working days after the IPO, subject to the final distribution schedule.

rANT is a tokenized asset linked to Anthropic, not direct ownership of Anthropic shares or the voting rights associated with them.

🤔 MY THOUGHTS

The refund process needs to be discussed because some people might assume committing $100,000 means they will automatically receive that amount in IPO exposure.

But the actual allocation could be considerably smaller, especially if demand exceeds the shares available through the platform.

In the Exclusive Earn feature, I would treat the interest on refunded funds as a separate benefit rather than a reason to commit more capital.

Personally, I would pay more attention to the final IPO valuation, underwriting fees, and how much exposure I am actually comfortable taking before deciding whether to participate.

For anyone considering Anthropic IPO Prime, the official page explains the subscription process and eligibility requirements: https://t.co/5IlsGhjsOh

The $100,000 commitment and 80% allocation shown here are hypothetical figures, not actual subscription results or promised returns.

Understanding how your funds are allocated, charged, and refunded matters just as much as getting access to the IPO itself.

text:
A combination of California Health & Safety Codes and selective interpretation by SF judges makes enforcement a round robin circus. The law requires:
- Actual sale, furnishing, transportation for sale, etc. (e.g., H&S 11352): Prosecutors must prove the defendant sold/furnished/transported (or offered to) a controlled substance, knew of its presence and nature, and (for transport) that there was a usable amount. Direct evidence of a transaction (observed hand-to-hand exchange of drugs for money, undercover buy-bust with marked bills, or similar) is the clearest proof.
- Possession for sale (e.g., H&S 11351 for certain narcotics, 11378 for meth): Must prove possession (actual or constructive), knowledge of the substance and its nature, a usable amount, and specific intent to sell. Intent is usually shown circumstantially via quantity beyond personal use, multiple small packages/baggies, scales, large amounts of cash (especially small bills), pay-owe notes, text messages, packaging materials, or observed transactions. There is no fixed weight threshold that automatically proves intent; it is case-specific.
- Loitering for drug activities (H&S 11532, a misdemeanor) is a tool SFPD has used more in recent crackdowns. It requires loitering in a public place with intent to commit a drug offense (sale, possession for sale, etc.). Intent can be shown by circumstances listed in the statute and SFPD guidance, such as:
•  Transferring small objects/packages for currency in a furtive manner
•  Acting as a lookout
•  Repeatedly beckoning to or exchanging money/small objects with passersby
•  Using drug-related signals/language
•  Prior related convictions or behavior, presence in a known drug area, etc.
Officers must document observations thoroughly (including body-worn camera or surveillance). There is no minimum number of circumstances required, but thin evidence often fails to support charges or convictions. Mass loitering arrests in sweeps have frequently resulted in citations, releases, or no charges.

text:
*🙏 Om Namo Venkatesaya 🙏*

*🪔 The Beginning of the 'Akasha Deepam' (Sky Lamp) 🪔*

🕉️🙏🙏🙏🙏🙏🙏🙏🙏🙏🙏🕉️

Why should an 'Akasha Deepam' be lit? What is its significance?

The month of Kartika is held in high regard and is deeply dear to both Shiva and Kesava (Vishnu).

🍃🌹As this month begins, an 'Akasha Deepam'—a 'sky lamp'—is hung from the *dhwajasthambham* (temple flagstaff). It consists of a round brass vessel with small perforations, filled with oil and lit as a lamp.

🪔 The Akasha Deepam illuminates the path for the *Pitru Devatas* (ancestral spirits)

🍃🌹Using a rope, this vessel is hoisted high and suspended from the top of the temple flagstaff. There is a specific reason why it is called an 'Akasha Deepam' (sky lamp) and why it is hung from the flagstaff.

🍃🌹According to the *Kartika Purana*, this lamp is lit for the sake of the *Pitru Devatas* who travel through the celestial realm. It is believed that, starting from the first day of the bright fortnight of the month of Kartika (*Kartika Shuddha Padyami*), the ancestral spirits journey back to their respective realms through the sky. The Akasha Deepam is lit in temples to help them clearly see their path.

🪔 The Akasha Deepam radiates the divine splendor of Shiva and Kesava to the entire world

🍃🌹There is another significant purpose behind lighting the Akasha Deepam. It serves as a symbol of the divine power of Shiva and Kesava; by lighting it atop the flagstaff, prayers are offered for its radiance to spread across the entire world. 🍃🌹 While lighting a lamp, devotees invoke Shiva and Keshava (Vishnu) by chanting "Damodaram Avahayami" and "Tryambakam Avahayami." In some regions, two separate lamps are lit—one for Shiva and one for Keshava—while in others, a single lamp is lit to invoke either of the two.

🍃🌹 Devotees believe that a lamp, infused with the radiance of both Shiva and Keshava, illuminates the entire world. The deeper, symbolic meaning is that the darkness of ignorance within society should be dispelled, allowing a spiritual light to shine brightly within each of us.

🍃🌹 The month of Kartika, a period in which the lamp holds immense significance, begins with the lighting of the *Akasha Deepam* (a lamp raised high toward the sky).

*🪔 The Significance of the Akasha Deepam*

🍃🌹 It is believed that lighting an *Akasha Deepam*, adding oil to it, or simply beholding and offering salutations to it, brings great spiritual merit (*punya*). It is thought that this practice not only removes the ignorance and lack of wisdom within us but also brings contentment to our ancestral spirits (*pitru devatas*).

🍃🌹 An *Akasha Deepam* can be lit not only in temples but also in every home. One should perform *puja* to the lamp, offer incense (*dhupa*) and food (*naivedya*), and bow down while remembering Shiva and Keshava. Afterward, the lamp is lit and suspended from a high pole using a rope.

🪔 The flame of the lamp is the Supreme Brahman (*Parabrahma*);
The lamp dispels all darkness. Everything is made possible through the lamp;
Salutations to Deepalakshmi (the Goddess in the form of a lamp).

*🙏 Om Namah Shivaya 🙏*
*🙏 Om Namo Narayanaya 🙏*

text:
“You are God’s Temple: Living Stones Built on Christ, the Source of Living Water”
————
Contact: enakhena@reborn.com

Ezekiel 47:1–2, 8–9, 12-:
Key Verse-: "I saw water flowing out from beneath the threshold of the temple... Wherever the river flows, every living creature that swarms shall live." 
Psalm 46:2–3, 5–6, 8–9-:
Key Verse-: "The waters of the river gladden the city of God, the holy dwelling of the Most High!" 
1 Corinthians 3:9–11, 16–17-:
Key Verse-: "Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwells in you? For the temple of God, which you are, is holy."  
John 2:13–22
Key Verse-: Jesus answered and said to them, 'Destroy this temple and in three days I will raise it up.' But he was speaking about the temple of his body." 

The Flowing Water of Grace (Ezekiel 4): The prophet envisions life-giving water flowing from the right side of the temple altar, bringing healing to salty deserts and dead waters. Ezekiel’s vision shows the temple as the source of life-giving water that transforms the barren and heals the dead. This prefigures the Church and the sacraments (especially Baptism and the Eucharist). The water flowing from the sanctuary points forward to the blood and water from Christ’s side on the Cross (John 19:34) and to the living water Jesus offers (John 7:37-38). This passage teaches us that genuine encounters with God should produce positive changes in our lives and in the lives of those around us.

When God’s grace flows through us:
  Hatred gives way to forgiveness. Dishonesty gives way to integrity. Pride gives way to humility. Despair gives way to hope.Selfishness gives way to generosity.
Spiritual emptiness gives way to renewed faith. (1 Corinthians 3): Apostle Paul shifts the definition of "temple" from limestone and gold to human lives. The Holy Spirit lives in you. Because your body and soul are consecrated, they demand reverence, purity, and intentional spiritual care. Paul teaches that the foundation is already laid: Jesus Christ. We are not spectators but living stones being built into a spiritual house. The Holy Spirit dwells in us individually and corporately; therefore the temple is holy and must not be destroyed by sin, division, or indifference.

John 2: When Jesus clears the marketplace in the Jerusalem temple, He demonstrates zeal for God's holiness. He reveals that true worship is no longer tied to one physical location, but to His Risen Body. This shows Jesus’ zeal for pure worship. The cleansing of the temple is an acted parable of judgment and renewal. Jesus identifies His Body as the true Temple—destroyed in the Passion and raised on the third day. The Church is the Body of Christ extended in time; every baptized person shares in that temple reality. Jesus’ cleansing invites an examination of conscience: What “marketplaces” (self-interest, distraction, worldly priorities) have we allowed into the sanctuary of our hearts or our parish communities?

PRAYERS & MEDITATION 

Heavenly Father, Source of every living grace, thank You for choosing to make Your home within my heart.  Cleanse me of everything that distracts me from true worship. Overturn the clutter of self-interest, anxiety, and sin, and rebuild my life on Jesus Christ, the only firm foundation. May Your Holy Spirit flow through my words and actions today like living water, bringing comfort, healing, and peace to everyone I meet. Keep me mindful of the sanctity of my body and the dignity of every person as Your living temple.Amen

text:
Weekly|Thoughts on Short/Mid/Long Terms, Texas Permitting, Cybersecurity, APP & Unity, Space Compute, Optical Demand

After one of the most violent market selloffs in recent years, we want to take a step back and consider the AI sector across different time horizons.

Over the long term, we remain excited about AI’s potential. Frontier labs continue to make meaningful progress toward AGI, with larger pretrained models delivering substantial capability gains. As reinforcement learning scales and data accumulates, general-purpose models are also expanding into areas previously served by specialized models, including robotics and video and audio generation. In our conversations with leading researchers, optimism about reaching AGI in 2028 or beyond is higher than we have previously encountered.

The medium-term picture, through roughly 2027, is harder to assess. Much of the leading labs’ revenue still comes from AI startups and large technology companies. For startups dependent on venture funding, how sustainable is their spending if macro conditions and funding availability deteriorate? Large technology companies are already optimizing token consumption: where does their spending settle, and what would drive renewed acceleration? Meanwhile, our enterprise surveys have consistently pointed to slower adoption than the market had hoped for. Taken together, these trends raise the possibility of a meaningful gap between the spending growth investors expect and what customers ultimately deliver.

On the semiconductor and hardware side, we are hearing more reports from the Asian supply chain of slower deliveries and procurement schedules. These warrant attention, though they do not yet establish order cuts. Are they mainly the result of product transitions and deployment timing, or early signs of tighter spending discipline? And how resilient would infrastructure investment prove if financing conditions tightened further, particularly for neoclouds?

These medium-term questions can coexist with a near-term rebound. Following such a sharp selloff, even modest improvements in fourth-quarter revenue expectations could matter if share prices already discount a much weaker spending outlook. A strong model release could provide a more credible catalyst, particularly if better capabilities translate into stronger paid demand and more durable pricing. We are not making a market-direction call. We do think it is important to remain open-minded as expectations reset and new evidence emerges.

There are also new areas worth watching closely. Our latest space compute work is one bright spot: progress in thermal design, supply-chain orders and launch planning is making orbital compute a more concrete engineering proposition. We see a path to roughly 0.5 GW of on-orbit capacity by the end of 2028 in our base case, and approximately 1 GW in an optimistic scenario, with thermal validation and launch cadence still critical. Cybersecurity remains another area where we see substantial opportunity. AI is accelerating vulnerability discovery and increasing the demands on defense, remediation and governance. The need is growing, but the timing of monetization matters: more attacks will not necessarily translate into an immediate revenue uplift for listed security vendors.

Beyond the AI infrastructure trade, AppLovin and Unity are a reminder that opportunities remain elsewhere. We have followed both companies closely through several quarters, and our channel work has captured important shifts in their competitive dynamics and operating momentum. Their strong results and post-earnings rallies reinforce the value of that sustained research. We will continue looking for and tracking opportunities across our coverage, including those outside the market’s dominant AI narrative.

This Week’s Reports

LLM 26Q4: Capabilities advance faster than commercial returns. Our deep dive examines frontier competition, falling task costs and AI-assisted research, with roughly 70% of leading labs’ compute spending still going toward uses other than paid inference.
https://t.co/8OcEtXUeo7

Space compute: Engineering progress makes orbital capacity more tangible. Our supply-chain work identifies 6,000 planned racks and a path to roughly 0.5 GW of on-orbit compute by end-2028 in the base case, or about 1 GW in the optimistic case, subject to launch cadence and thermal validation.
https://t.co/legnQgLRlf

Cybersecurity: Customers still favor existing cloud and security platforms. Our latest checks put remediation, response and governance at the center of spending, with limited near-term budget uplift despite faster AI-driven vulnerability discovery.
https://t.co/3GhAfN6QHb

Texas AIDC: Permitting uncertainty rises after the election. We maintain our 2027 delivery forecast for now, but a prolonged freeze could reduce deliverable supply by another 2–3 GW of IT capacity in our downside scenario.
https://t.co/C3bqOXp6vQ

Preview & Review | APP & Unity 26Q3: Both grow through the competitive dispute. Following our channel checks on bidding and data access, AppLovin returned to a beat-and-raise with 55% revenue growth, while Unity’s Vector grew 40% sequentially against guidance of roughly 20%.
https://t.co/ZShPLwFBHZ
https://t.co/fnCZU4lc3s
https://t.co/Rf4vwB3z2R

Review | DDOG 26Q3: Pricing and commitments complicate the guide. Revenue grew 35.2%, with non-AI growth accelerating for a fifth quarter, but minimum commitments and lower renewal pricing held the Q4 growth guide to 25–26%.
https://t.co/Wxd492U3a4

Review | PLTR FY26Q3: Growth stays strong as bookings soften. Revenue rose 96% and Q4 guidance implies roughly 88% growth; shorter contracts and repricing flexibility offer a possible explanation for softer bookings without establishing weaker underlying demand.
https://t.co/AMRiyzTpYk

INIO: The installed base supports a long service tail. Our initiation examines roughly 44 GW of installed capacity, $8bn of equipment backlog and 10–15-year service relationships, alongside delivery execution and the November lock-up expiry.

text:
Lakewood Man Accused of Running $5.2 Million AI Investment Scheme, Leaving Investors With Millions in Losses

LAKEWOOD, Colo. | November 8, 2026

A Lakewood man is facing a lawsuit filed by Colorado regulators after allegedly collecting more than $5.2 million from investors through an artificial intelligence investment operation that state attorneys describe as a Ponzi-like scheme.

Michael Cole, a radiologist, allegedly convinced 14 investors, including family members and former colleagues, to invest in his company, Sage Income LLC, by promising unusually high returns through artificial intelligence software designed to trade stocks.

According to a complaint filed Wednesday in Denver District Court, Cole claimed his proprietary AI algorithm could generate higher-than-average market returns and had undergone extensive testing.

State investigators allege those representations were false.

Millions Collected, Millions Lost

According to the lawsuit, Cole raised approximately $5.2 million through promissory notes issued by Sage Income LLC.

Investors were told their money would be used to purchase securities through an AI-powered trading system.

However, investigators examining the company’s financial records reportedly discovered a different financial picture.

Bank records cited in the complaint indicate Sage Income consistently lost money every month between November 2019 and December 2024.

Rather than generating profits through successful trading, the company allegedly used money from new investors and additional funds supplied by Cole to make payments to existing investors.

State attorneys described the operation as a “Ponzi-like scheme.”

By February 2025, when Sage Income filed for bankruptcy, the 14 investors had collectively lost more than $3.9 million, according to the complaint.

Family Members Among Alleged Victims

The lawsuit alleges Cole’s investors included his own brother, parents, and former business associates.

Before establishing Sage Income LLC in September 2019, Cole reportedly owed approximately $1.3 million to three former business partners, including two family members, following the dissolution of an earlier company called Cole Capital LLC.

Investigators allege Cole continued soliciting investments despite the company’s ongoing financial losses.

Bank records also allegedly revealed that Cole transferred some investor money into his personal bank account and used the funds to repay an unrelated loan.

Cole told investigators that investors’ money had been used to develop and train the AI trading software, according to the complaint.

State Regulators Allege Securities Violations

Colorado officials say Cole was not licensed to offer or sell securities in the state.

The lawsuit alleges he violated Colorado securities laws while soliciting investments through promissory notes.

Colorado Securities Commissioner Tung Chan criticized the alleged operation.

“We believe that Mr. Cole used the promise of AI investing to defraud Coloradans, including his own brother, parents and colleagues,” Chan said in a statement.

Chan also warned that emerging technologies are increasingly being used to promote familiar investment scams.

“We have seen a lot of the same old scams that mask themselves behind the excitement of new technology like AI.”

The commissioner urged investors to research opportunities carefully before committing money, particularly when promised returns appear unusually attractive.

Artificial Intelligence Used as Investment Pitch

The allegations highlight concerns about investment schemes that use artificial intelligence as a selling point.

According to the complaint, Cole repeatedly assured investors that his software had been extensively tested and that Sage Income was financially stable.

State attorneys described those statements as “flagrantly dishonest.”

Investigators allege the company was consistently losing money while continuing to attract investors with promises of AI-generated profits.

Lawsuit Pending

The allegations remain part of a civil lawsuit and have not been established as findings of wrongdoing by a court.

The Denver Post reported that Cole could not be reached for comment Saturday.

The case raises questions about investor protections, financial transparency, and the use of emerging technologies to market investment opportunities.

For the 14 investors involved, the alleged losses total more than $3.9 million, with several of those affected reportedly belonging to Cole’s own family.

The Colorado Division of Securities is pursuing the allegations through the courts.

Source: The Denver Post, reporting on a Colorado securities enforcement complaint filed in Denver District Court.

text:
🤰🏻🤰🏽🤰🏿 Pregnancy Days 253 to 259 (Week 37): Phase Three: Early Term
📚 Source: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists. General pregnancy education only, not medical advice. Always talk with your doctor or midwife.
🔊 Your baby reaches early term this week and could be born any day. But the brain and lungs are still being finished. And soon you will meet your baby's first cry. Which song will calm it, and how do lullabies, nursery rhymes, and phonic songs help? Read on.

🗓️ Week 37 at a Glance
Week 37 is pregnancy days 253 to 259, counted from the first day of your last period, the same count your doctor, midwife, and pregnancy calculator use. If conception happened around day 14, your baby is between 239 and 245 days old. In longer or shorter cycles, these days shift a little.
This is the week of early term. Your baby could be born any day now and is likely to do well. But the brain and lungs keep maturing right up to full term. Your baby practices grasping, sucking, and turning toward light, and keeps adding fat.
Your baby is about 19 inches from head to heel and weighs about 6 1/3 pounds, about the size of a small watermelon. Three weeks remain until your due date.

🗓️ The Week, Day by Day
Here is the week counted in days after conception. In a 28-day cycle, add 14 to find your pregnancy day. Babies arrive in their own time, so read this as a guide.
Days 239 and 240 (pregnancy days 253 and 254): Your baby reaches early term. The lungs keep making surfactant.
Days 241 and 242 (days 255 and 256): The brain keeps growing, adding connections every day.
Day 243 (day 257): Your baby practices grasping, sucking, and turning the head toward light.
Day 244 (day 258): Fat keeps building, helping your baby stay warm after birth.
Day 245 (day 259): Your baby weighs about 6 1/3 pounds and is about 19 inches from head to heel.

🗓️ What "Term" Means
Doctors use special names for babies born in the last weeks of pregnancy:
Early term: 37 weeks through 38 weeks and 6 days.
Full term: 39 weeks through 40 weeks and 6 days.
Late term: 41 weeks through 41 weeks and 6 days.
Post-term: 42 weeks and beyond.
Babies born at early term usually do well. But research shows that babies born at full term, 39 weeks or later, have fewer problems with breathing, feeding, and staying warm. That is why doctors recommend that a planned birth, by induction or cesarean, not happen before 39 weeks unless there is a medical reason.
If your baby comes on their own in early term, that is God's timing. If you are offered a planned birth, ask your doctor why and when.

🧠 Still Growing
Even though your baby looks ready, important growth is still happening. The brain grows a great deal in the last weeks of pregnancy. The lungs keep making surfactant. Fat keeps building. The ability to feed and to keep warm keeps getting stronger.
Every day in the womb now is a day of finishing touches. Try to enjoy these days. Rest. Sing. Pray. Let your baby finish.

🖐️ Grasping and Rooting
Your baby practices the reflexes that will be needed after birth. The grasp reflex lets your baby wrap fingers tightly around anything placed in the palm. The rooting reflex turns your baby's head toward a touch on the cheek. The sucking reflex is strong.
After birth, you will see all of these. Place your finger in your baby's palm and feel the grip. Stroke the cheek and watch your baby turn to feed. These reflexes are God's built-in tools to help your baby survive and bond in the first weeks.

😢 Why Newborns Cry
Crying is how a newborn speaks. Your baby will cry when hungry, wet, tired, too hot or cold, uncomfortable, or simply wanting to be held. Many babies also have a fussy time each day, often in the evening.
Crying usually increases over the first weeks and often peaks around six weeks of age, then slowly gets better. This is normal. It does not mean you are doing something wrong.
When your baby cries, check the basics: hunger, diaper, temperature, burping. Then try comfort: hold your baby close, sway or rock, make a gentle shushing sound, and sing a familiar song. If you ever feel frustrated, it is okay to lay your baby safely on their back in the crib and step away for a few minutes to calm down. Never shake a baby. Call your baby's doctor if the crying seems unusual or comes with fever, poor feeding, or other signs of illness.
“In the manner of one whom a mother caresses, so will I console you. And you will be consoled in Jerusalem.” (Isaiah 66:13, CPDV)
“James Monroe was born April 28, 1758. His time as president of the United States was remembered as the "Era of Good Feelings," a season of calm after years of conflict.”

🎶 Songs That Soothe
Your baby has heard your weekly songs for months. After birth, those songs may be some of your best tools for comfort. Studies show newborns respond to sounds and voices they heard often before birth.
Slow, steady singing, gentle swaying, and close holding together can help calm a crying baby. The rhythm of your heartbeat, which your baby has heard every day, is also comforting, so hold your baby against your chest.
Choose one or two songs to be your baby's comfort songs. Sing them every time your baby is upset. Over the weeks, your baby will learn that these songs mean "you are safe."
“In peace itself, I will sleep and I will rest. For you, O Lord, have established me singularly in hope.” (Psalm 4:8; CPDV 4:9)
“Bing Crosby was born May 3, 1903. His gentle singing of an Irish lullaby in the 1944 film Going My Way became a favorite, and his calm, warm voice comforted listeners for decades.”

🔤 Phase Three: Comfort Words
Phase Three has given you many kinds of words and your first sentences. This week, sing comfort words: "shh," "safe," "near," "I'm here," "it's okay," "rest."
Build each one from your First Sounds list. "Shh" is the "sh" phonogram, held long and soft. "Safe" is "s," "a," "f," "e." "Near" is "n" and "ear." "Here" is "h" and "ere." Sing each one slowly on the melody of the weekly song.
Put them together into a comfort song: "Shh, shh, I'm here. You are safe, my dear." Sing it every day this week, softly and slowly. After birth, sing it when your baby cries. Comfort songs are the oldest kind of lullabies and nursery rhymes. They are phonic songs, baby music, and the gentlest kids music there is.
“Write the vision and explain it on tablets.” (Habakkuk 2:2, CPDV)
“Morgan Freeman was born June 1, 1937. He worked patiently for many years on stage before his big film roles came in his fifties, and his calm, steady voice became one of the most recognized in the world.”

💧 When Your Water Breaks
The amniotic sac can break before or during labor. It may come as a sudden gush or a slow trickle. The fluid is usually clear or pale and has little smell.
If you think your water has broken, call your doctor or midwife right away, even if you are not having tightenings. Note the time, the color of the fluid, and whether it has a smell. Tell your doctor right away if the fluid is green or brown, or if you feel something in the vagina.
Do not put anything in the vagina after your water breaks. Your doctor will tell you whether to come in now or wait at home.

🔔 Bloody Show and the Mucus Plug
During pregnancy, a thick plug of mucus seals the opening of the cervix. As the cervix begins to soften and open, the plug may come out. You may see thick mucus, sometimes tinged pink, red, or brown. This is called bloody show.
It can happen days or even weeks before labor, or during labor itself. It is a sign that your body is getting ready. Call your doctor if you have bright red bleeding like a period, or heavy bleeding, which is not normal bloody show.

🤰 Your Body at Thirty-Seven Weeks
Your body is preparing for birth. You may feel more pressure in the pelvis, more frequent Braxton Hicks tightenings, and lower back aches. You may feel an urge to clean and organize.
Sleep may be hard. Get up slowly, rest during the day, and keep pillows close. Keep walking gently if your doctor says it is safe.

🏠 Your Coming-Home Plan
The first days home with a newborn go best with a simple plan. Decide ahead of time how many visitors you want and when. Ask visitors to wash their hands, to stay home if they are sick, and to help with a chore or bring a meal.
Sleep when you can, even during the day. Remember safe sleep: your baby on the back, in a crib or bassinet with a firm, flat mattress and nothing else in it, in your room. Keep the car seat for the car, not for sleep at home.
Your baby will usually see a doctor within a few days of going home. Write the appointment in your journal, along with your questions.

🤝 Support in Labor
Support during labor makes a real difference. Studies show that women who have steady support from a person they trust often feel more satisfied with their birth. That person may be Dad, a family member, a friend, or a trained labor helper called a doula.
Talk with your support person now about what helps you: words of encouragement, quiet, a hand to hold, a back rub, cool cloths, music, prayer. Put the weekly songs and your headphones in your bag so familiar music is there with you.

🍯 Never Honey Before One
Never give honey to a baby under one year old, not even a tiny taste on a pacifier. Honey can carry spores that cause infant botulism, a serious illness in babies.
Your baby needs only breast milk or formula for about the first six months. Do not give water, juice, or cereal in a bottle unless your baby's doctor tells you to. After about six months, your baby's doctor will guide you on starting solid foods.

🚗 Using the Car Seat Correctly
Practice buckling a doll or stuffed animal in the car seat before birth. The harness straps should be snug, so you cannot pinch extra strap at the shoulder. The chest clip should sit at armpit level. The straps for a rear-facing seat should come from at or just below your baby's shoulders.
Do not put your baby in the car seat in a bulky coat or snowsuit, because it can make the straps too loose in a crash. Instead, buckle your baby in normal clothes and put a blanket over the straps. Use the car seat for car rides, not as a place for your baby to sleep at home.

🫂 Skin-to-Skin With Dad
Skin-to-skin contact is not just for mothers. Dads can hold the baby on a bare chest too. It helps keep the baby warm and calm and helps dads bond with their newborn.
This can be especially helpful if Mom is recovering from a cesarean or needs rest. Dad, take off your shirt, hold your baby in just a diaper against your chest, cover both of you with a blanket, and sing the weekly song. Your baby will feel your heartbeat and hear your voice, the same voice heard for months through the womb.

🛌 Safe Sleep Products to Avoid
Many products sold for babies are not safe for sleep. Avoid inclined sleepers, sleep positioners, wedges, crib bumpers, and weighted sleep sacks or blankets. Do not let your baby sleep in a car seat, swing, or bouncer for long periods outside the car.
Safe sleep is simple: on the back, in a crib, bassinet, or play yard that meets current safety standards, on a firm, flat mattress with a fitted sheet, and nothing else in the sleep space. Keep the baby in your room, but not in your bed.

📖 Psalms for the Waiting
The book of Psalms is full of prayers for waiting, trusting, and finding peace. In these last weeks, read one psalm each day. Psalm 23 speaks of the Shepherd who leads. Psalm 121 speaks of the God who watches over you. Psalm 127 speaks of children as a gift from God. Psalm 139 speaks of how God formed your baby in the womb.
Read them out loud, so your baby hears your voice. Pray them back to God in your own words. Write one line from each in your journal.

🌡️ Taking Your Baby's Temperature
Learn how to take your baby's temperature before you need to. For babies, a temperature taken in the bottom with a digital thermometer is most accurate. Put a little petroleum jelly on the tip, gently insert it about half an inch, and hold it until it beeps.
For a baby under three months, a temperature of 100.4 degrees Fahrenheit or higher is a fever. Call your baby's doctor right away. Do not give any medicine to a newborn unless your baby's doctor tells you to.

🏠 Gentle Rules for the First Month
Many families set a few gentle rules for the first month: wash hands before holding the baby, no visitors who are sick, no smoking anywhere near the baby, short visits, and quiet evenings.
Talk about these rules with Dad and share them kindly with family and friends before the birth. Most people are happy to help protect a newborn when they know what you need.

🧳 Final Bag Check
Take one more look at your hospital bag. Is your ID there? Your insurance card and birth preferences? Your phone charger and headphones? Clothes for you and the baby to wear home? Is the car seat installed in the car?
Add anything you forgot, and put the bag where it is easy to grab. Then let it go. You are as ready as you can be.

🙏 Asking for Prayer
Ask your church family to pray for you in these final weeks: for a safe labor, a healthy baby, a quick recovery, and peace. Give them a simple way to know when labor starts, such as a message from Dad or a family member.
Knowing that people are praying for you can bring great peace. And after birth, they can pray for the newborn days too.

🧼 Cleaning Feeding Supplies
If you use bottles or a breast pump, clean all the parts after every use. Take them apart, rinse them, and wash them in hot, soapy water with a brush set aside just for baby items, or in the dishwasher if the parts are dishwasher-safe. Let them air-dry on a clean towel or rack.
For babies under three months, born early, or with weak immune systems, many experts suggest sanitizing feeding items at least once a day, by boiling, steaming, or using the dishwasher's sanitize setting. Keep your hands clean when preparing bottles.

🌱 Accepting Your Limits
In the last weeks of pregnancy and the first weeks after birth, you will not be able to do everything you used to do. That is not failure. It is a season.
Make a short list of what truly matters each day: feeding, resting, healing, and loving your baby. Let other things wait or let others help. God gives strength for each day, not for every task you can imagine. Rest in that.

🧸 Tummy Time From the Start
Once your baby is home, short times of tummy time while awake and watched help your baby build neck, shoulder, and arm strength. Start with a minute or two a few times a day, on a blanket on the floor or on your chest. Get down at eye level, smile, and sing.
Always put your baby on the back to sleep, but give tummy time when your baby is awake and you are right there. Over the weeks, your baby will lift the head higher and longer.

💌 A Letter for the Birth Day
Write a short letter to your baby to read on the day of birth. Tell your baby how long you have waited, what you hope for their life, and how much you already love them. Put it in your hospital bag. Read it aloud after your baby is born. Then save it in your journal for your child to read one day.

🌤️ Gentle Mornings
Start each morning in these last weeks gently. Before you check your phone, put your hand on your belly and thank God for one more day. Sing the weekly song once, softly. Then begin your day. A gentle morning sets a calm tone for whatever the day brings.

🧸 Practicing Calm With a Doll
If you have never cared for a newborn, practice with a doll or a stuffed animal. Practice holding it with the head supported, swaddling it, buckling it in the car seat, and rocking it while you sing the comfort song. Older children love to help with this practice. It builds confidence for the real thing.

🥗 Body: Caring for the Home This Week
This week, eat light, nourishing meals that are easy on your stomach. Keep up protein, whole grains, fruits, vegetables, and calcium foods. Keep easy snacks ready for early labor, like crackers, fruit, and yogurt, and drink water often.
Keep up safe food habits. Cook meats, chicken, eggs, and seafood thoroughly. Rinse produce. Choose pasteurized dairy. Heat deli meats until steaming. Pick low-mercury fish, and avoid shark, swordfish, king mackerel, and tilefish.
No amount of alcohol is known to be safe in pregnancy. Avoid smoking, vaping, and secondhand smoke. Keep caffeine under 200 mg a day. Ask before any medicine, herb, or supplement, and stay gently active if your doctor approves.

🚨 Signs to Call About Now
Call your doctor or midwife right away if your water breaks, if your baby is moving much less than usual, or if you have bright red bleeding.
Also call when tightenings are regular and getting closer together, following your doctor's instructions, or right away for a severe headache, vision changes, sudden swelling of the face or hands, pain high on the right side of the belly, or a fever.
Keep the bag by the door and the car ready.

👨 For Dad: The Calm Voice
Dad, your baby will cry, and so may she. Your calm voice can help both of them. Practice the comfort song this week: "Shh, shh, I'm here. You are safe, my dear."
Learn how to soothe a baby: hold close, sway, shush, sing. Plan with her how you will share the night wakings, so neither of you is worn out alone.
Be ready for labor. Know the route, keep the gas tank full, and keep your phone charged. When it is time, your calm voice will matter more than anything.

👵 For Grandparents and Siblings
Big brothers and sisters can learn that babies cry, and that it is okay. Teach them the comfort song so they can help sing it to the baby.
Grandparents can share how they calmed their own babies. Write their tips in the journal. They may be the very thing that works.

🎶 One Song, Three Ways: Week 37
Every week has one GUP song, learned three different ways. A good preschool teacher never teaches an important lesson only once. Teach it three ways, and it is remembered.
Hear it. In the morning, listen once with your eyes closed. Thank God for bringing your baby to early term.
Hum it. At midday, put on headphones and hum along. Then sing "Shh, shh, I'm here. You are safe, my dear" to the tune, very softly.
Write it. In the evening, listen with your Pregnancy Journal open. Write the phonograms you hear, and write your comfort song in your journal.
GUP songs are baby music with a purpose: gentle like lullabies, repeating like nursery rhymes, and full of the phonic songs that become the building blocks of reading.

📓 Your Pregnancy Journal: Week-37 Pages
On your Word List page, add comfort words and your comfort song.
On a "Comfort Plan" page, write the songs you will use to calm your baby and the soothing tips grandparents shared.
Keep your "Daily Movement" page going. Write what to do if your water breaks, and add a prayer of patience for the last weeks.

🧭 God's GPS
Waiting is hard. You may want your baby to come now. Or you may want just a little more time. Neither choice is yours to make. God knows the day.
You make the plans, and God directs the steps. Waiting on Him is not wasted time. It is faith.
“The heart of man disposes his way. But it is for the Lord to direct his steps.” (Proverbs 16:9, CPDV)
“Jim Abbott was born September 19, 1967. Born without a right hand, he learned to throw and catch with one hand and pitched a no-hitter for the New York Yankees in 1993.”

🙏 A Prayer for Week 37
"Father God, thank You for bringing our baby to early term. Thank You for every day of growth that remains, for a brain and lungs still being finished, and for reflexes ready to grip and feed.
Give us patience to wait for Your timing. Comfort us as a mother comforts her child, so we can comfort our baby. When our baby cries, let our voices bring peace. Refresh us, and direct our steps to the day we meet. In Jesus' name, amen."

❓ Questions Parents Ask
Is my baby ready to be born? Babies born at early term usually do well, but the brain and lungs keep maturing. Full term, 39 weeks or later, is best for a planned birth unless there is a medical reason.
What should I do if my water breaks? Call your doctor or midwife right away. Note the time and the color of the fluid. Do not put anything in the vagina.
What is bloody show? A thick, sometimes pink or brown mucus as the cervix softens. Call your doctor for bright red or heavy bleeding.
How will I calm my crying baby? Check hunger, diaper, and temperature. Then hold close, sway, shush, and sing a familiar song. Never shake a baby.
When do I call my doctor right away? Call if your water breaks, for much less movement than usual, bright red bleeding, regular tightenings as your doctor instructed, a severe headache, vision changes, sudden swelling, or a fever.

✅ Your Week-37 Checklist
I took my prenatal vitamin every day. I noticed my baby's movements daily. I know what to do if my water breaks. I know the difference between bloody show and bleeding.
I heard, hummed, and wrote this week's one song every day. I sang comfort words and a comfort song. I added them to my Word List. Dad practiced the calm voice. The family learned the comfort song.

🎵 Why We Sing
Every GLAL lesson comes with its own baby music. These phonic songs are made to be sung by Mom, Dad, and the whole family, so your baby learns your real voices. Like the lullabies and nursery rhymes you grew up with, they are simple kids music that a newborn will hear again and again after birth. Sing this week's song today, and let it become the first kids music in your home.

📚 Source: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists. General pregnancy education only, not medical advice. Always talk with your doctor or midwife.

text:
Globalism is not based on free markets nor do globalists believe in free markets. Capitalism and globalism are not the same things. 

Free markets absolutely reject the initation of force by definition and this is one of my biggest contentions with classical liberalism.

Yes Smith said that the poor could be "driven by want, and prompted by envy, to invade his possessions." However, he also recognised that the wealthy could be driven by avarice and ambition, which could equally threaten the property of others. Smith understood that private property requires legal protection, that inequality creates tensions, and that government can emerge partly to protect accumulated wealth. He was explaining both the necessity of property rights and the unequal power relations that can accompany them. Those are two sides of his argument, not mutually exclusive interpretations. He was not suggesting the use of force upon the poor under a free market system. That would be a misinterpretation of his words. However....

For me Classical liberalism contains principles worth defending but not within the lens of classical liberalism, particularly private property, individual liberty and voluntary association, which have important historical connections to Christian moral thought. However, I believe classical liberalism fundamentally contradicts itself in its advocacy of the state, regardless of how small or limited that state might be. How can a political philosophy claim to uphold private property and voluntary association while legitimising an institution that can override both through force? My objection isn't simply that the state is too large. It is that the state's coercive foundations are fundamentally at odds with the very principles classical liberalism claims to defend. One cannot consistently defend individual liberty and private property while granting an institution the authority to violate those same rights. This is where the initation of force exists, not in the free market but in Adam Smiths and the classical liberal endorsement of state power.

To address your question on Inequality (and hopefully answer a few others along the way). It is a natural part of human existence. People differ in intelligence, abilities, ambitions, circumstances and achievements. Some will accumulate more wealth, some will enjoy better health, and others will excel in areas where their peers do not. Inequality of outcome is not, in itself, evidence of injustice. The important question is how those outcomes came about. Attempts to impose equality of outcome require interference with people's choices and property. When that interference involves coercion, it raises serious moral questions. Envy of what others possess is not a justification for taking it.

Capitalism accepts unequal outcomes and offers an alternative to enforced equality: if you want something, provide something of value that others voluntarily wish to exchange for it. Through private property, voluntary association, competition and trade, individuals pursue their own interests while creating value for others. This isn't a perfect meritocracy, nothing can ever be perfect and their will always be challenges but how a free voluntary society solves such challenges of monopoly and inheritence etc is for them to decide. It is not as if our State run democracies are doing it particularly well currently. "Compared to what?" is always a good question to ask. 

A genuinely competitive free market rewards the provision of goods and services that people voluntarily choose to purchase, rather than outcomes imposed by political authority. That is the crucial and important take away.

text:
Democracy’s Promise and Its Fatal Flaw

Democracy rests on a simple and appealing principle: every adult citizen holds an equal vote, giving each person a formal share of political power. In theory, this equalizes influence and protects against tyranny by ensuring that no single group can permanently dominate. In practice, however, people are not interchangeable. They differ in wealth, productivity, risk tolerance, time horizons, and the material conditions of their lives. These differences produce systematically divergent preferences about the size and role of government. When the franchise is universal and equal, the numerical majority—typically those with less accumulated wealth—can impose policies that serve their immediate interests while eroding the incentives that generate prosperity. Over time, this dynamic pushes democratic societies toward socialism, economic stagnation, and, ultimately, the collapse of democracy itself into authoritarian rule.

The mechanism is straightforward. Individuals with lower incomes or fewer assets rationally favor higher progressive taxation, expanded transfer payments, and publicly provided goods such as healthcare, housing, and education at little or no direct cost to themselves. Because these voters outnumber those who bear the primary tax burden, electoral competition rewards parties and candidates who promise redistribution. Once enacted, such policies raise the marginal cost of investment, entrepreneurship, and high-effort work. Capital becomes more mobile or simply less productive; innovation slows; and the taxable base shrinks. Governments respond by raising rates further or expanding regulation, accelerating the cycle. What begins as compassionate social insurance gradually evolves into a system in which the state assumes ever-larger responsibility for economic outcomes—the defining feature of socialism.

History illustrates this pattern with striking clarity. In the late Roman Republic, populist leaders such as the Gracchi brothers and later Publius Clodius expanded the grain dole—state-subsidized or free distributions of wheat to urban citizens—to secure the support of the growing masses. These measures, combined with broader land reforms and clientelist politics, shifted power toward those dependent on public provision. The resulting fiscal strain, factional violence, and erosion of property rights fueled decades of civil war, culminating in the end of republican institutions and the establishment of imperial autocracy under Augustus. What began as democratic responsiveness to the many ended in the concentration of power in one man.

A modern parallel appears in Venezuela. Hugo Chávez was elected president in 1998 through free and competitive elections, capitalizing on widespread discontent with inequality. He implemented expansive redistributive programs funded by oil revenues, nationalized key industries, imposed price controls, and steadily concentrated authority under the banner of “21st-century socialism.” As private investment fled and production collapsed, economic crisis deepened. Under his successor, Nicolás Maduro, the regime completed the transition: elections became neither free nor fair, opposition was suppressed, and authoritarian rule replaced the democracy that had initially empowered the project.

Argentina offers a recurring version of the same dynamic. Juan Perón’s democratic election in 1946 ushered in Peronism—a populist system of wage hikes, social benefits, nationalizations, and protectionism aimed at the urban working majority. These policies generated short-term gains for supporters but produced chronic inflation, capital flight, and stagnation. The pattern repeated across decades: Peronist governments returned via the ballot box, expanded redistribution, and were periodically interrupted by military interventions when the economic consequences became unsustainable. Democracy repeatedly empowered the redistributive impulse, yet the underlying incentives never stabilized into lasting prosperity or institutional resilience.

In each case, the equal franchise allowed the numerical majority to enact policies that discouraged the creation of wealth. As private enterprise contracted, dependence on the state grew, reinforcing the electoral coalition that demanded still more intervention. When growth faltered and fiscal pressures mounted, political leaders faced incentives to centralize power, suppress dissent, and manage scarcity through command rather than markets. At that point, formal democratic institutions became hollow: elections continued in form, but meaningful choice disappeared. Democracy, having undermined the productive foundations that sustained it, yielded to dictatorship.

This outcome is not the result of malice or conspiracy. It follows from the rational pursuit of self-interest under rules that treat unequal people as politically identical. Equal voting power in the presence of unequal economic stakes creates a structural bias toward consumption of the present over investment in the future.

Reforming the Franchise to Preserve Ordered Liberty

If the equal vote is the engine of the problem, the solution lies in reforming the voting system so that political influence more closely tracks the contribution of resources and the assumption of risk. One coherent approach is to weight votes according to net tax contributions or a broader measure of economic stakeholding—property ownership, earned income, or a combination thereof—while retaining universal adult suffrage as a baseline right. Under such a system, those who fund the state would possess proportionally greater say over how its resources are allocated. This would raise the political cost of purely redistributive measures and restore incentives for productive activity.

Alternative or complementary reforms could include dual chambers in which one house is elected on an equal-franchise basis and the other is selected by economic contribution or by regional economic output; supermajority requirements for tax increases or new entitlement programs; or constitutional limits that require any expansion of the welfare state to be financed by concurrent reductions elsewhere. The precise design matters less than the principle: political power should not be entirely decoupled from the creation of the wealth that sustains the polity.

Such reforms are not a rejection of democracy but an attempt to make it sustainable. By aligning voting weight more closely with the capacity to bear the consequences of policy, a society can retain popular accountability while protecting the conditions—private property, capital accumulation, and voluntary exchange—that make broad prosperity and genuine self-government possible. Without some correction of this kind, the internal logic of equal-franchise democracy continues to favor the progressive conversion of a free economy into a managed one, and of a free polity into an unfree one. The historical record, from ancient Rome to contemporary Venezuela and Argentina, shows that the danger is neither abstract nor remote.

text:
Bulk Production Cleared for Indian Army's 307 ATAGS, Bharat Forge and TASL to Share 60:40 Order with Deliveries Expected from FY2028

To bridge the gap between the 307 ATAGS currently on order and the overarching need for mass artillery replacement, the Ministry of Defence is exploring dual strategies.

Future procurements are expected to focus heavily on lighter artillery systems that fit seamlessly within the military's existing 15-ton logistical limit.

Simultaneously, there are ongoing discussions regarding the development of a weight-reduced variant of the ATAGS under the domestic 'Buy Indian-IDDM' framework, which would offer the same cutting-edge firepower in a more mobile package.

Despite the weight-related deployment trade-offs, the ATAGS is widely recognised as a formidable asset with low maintenance overhead.

Its technical superiority has already been validated globally, highlighted by its successful export to the Armenian Ground Forces.

As the domestic production lines prepare to roll out the 307 guns, the ATAGS stands as a definitive success story for India's indigenous defence capabilities.India’s push for self-reliance in military manufacturing has reached a crucial milestone.

The indigenous 155mm/52-calibre Advanced Towed Artillery Gun System (ATAGS) has received bulk production clearance, unlocking the final phase before mass manufacturing begins.

This development clears the path for the Indian Army to significantly upgrade its long-range firepower, with the first batch of these modern howitzers scheduled to enter active service in the first quarter of the financial year 2028.The Production Blueprint​
The groundwork for this capability leap was established in March 2025, when the Ministry of Defence signed a contract worth approximately ₹6,900 crore to procure 307 ATAGS units, alongside highly specialised 6x6 towing vehicles.

Designed by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO), the production responsibilities have been entrusted to two private sector defence giants: Bharat Forge and Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL).

Under the finalised arrangement, Bharat Forge is responsible for 60 percent of the order, which translates to 184 guns, while TASL will manufacture the remaining 40 percent.

With production clearance now secured, manufacturing activities are set to gain momentum late next year.

Once deliveries begin in early FY2028, the industry expects a steady, phased handover of the guns over a four-year timeframe, carefully aligned with the Army’s regimen for troop training and structural deployment.Analysing the Procurement: Why Only 307?​
A notable aspect of this development is the order size. While the Indian Army’s total requirement for towed artillery is estimated to be between 1,400 and 1,500 guns, the current ATAGS procurement is capped at 307 units.

This limitation is rooted in logistical and infrastructural realities rather than the weapon's combat performance.

The ATAGS is a highly sophisticated platform equipped with an all-electric drive, automated ammunition handling, and an advanced fire-control system.

This heavy reliance on electromechanical automation ensures rapid deployment and high reliability but pushes the system's weight to around 18 tons.

The Indian Army’s existing towing infrastructure, designed over decades, is primarily optimised to handle artillery platforms weighing under 15 tons.

Integrating the heavier ATAGS requires the parallel induction of specialised high-mobility towing vehicles, meaning broader deployment necessitates a significant overhaul of existing logistical support.

text:
DEMOCRATS MAKE SWEEPING GUBERNATORIAL GAINS DURING TRUMP'S TWO TERMS IN OFFICE

During Trump's first term, Democrats flipped governorships in Wisconsin, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Kansas, Nevada, Illinois, New Mexico, Maine, New Jersey and Kentucky. Republicans made two gains of their own, taking control of West Virginia in 2017 after Governor Jim Justice switched parties and flipping Montana in 2020.

The trend has continued into Trump's second term, with Democrats making major gains in the midterms, flipping Republican-held governorships in Texas, Georgia, Ohio, Iowa and Nevada.

In Texas, Gina Hinojosa became the first Democrat elected governor since Ann Richards in 1990. Georgia also elected its first Democratic governor in nearly three decades, with Keisha Lance Bottoms becoming the first Democrat to win since Roy Barnes in 1998.

Democrats broke long losing streaks in Ohio and Iowa, where the party had not won a governor's race since 2006. Nevada, meanwhile, returned to Democratic control after Republicans flipped the state in 2022.

The results leave Democrats controlling a majority of governorships nationwide for the first time since 2010, a considerable change from January 2017, when Republicans held 33 governor's offices as Trump entered the White House.
